examples.why: "diagrama de Circuit" is the standard term "diagrama de circuito" half-left in English, and the same sentence correctly writes "las puertas" — the split is visible within one line.

examples.source: the circles and vertical line connecting the two qubits is a CNOT gate … What are the two gates that create the Bell state here?
examples.suggested: … es una puerta CNOT … ¿Cuáles son las dos puertas que crean el estado de Bell aquí?
examples.translation: los círculos y la línea vertical que conecta los dos qubits es un Gate CNOT … ¿Cuáles son los dos Gates que crean el estado de Bell aquí?
examples.why: "Gate" leaks in body text and in a comprehension question whose own answer immediately says "Una puerta H … una puerta CX", so the learner sees the question and its answer using two different words for the same object.

examples.source: to put the first qubit into an equal superposition … device calibration drifts over time
examples.suggested: para poner el primer qubit en una superposición equiprobable … la calibración del dispositivo se desvía con el tiempo
examples.translation: para poner el primer qubit en una superposición uniforme (equiprobable) … la calibración del dispositivo se desvía (deriva) con el tiempo
examples.why: Parenthetical double glosses that the English does not have; a native technical writer would commit to one term rather than hedging with a synonym in parentheses, which reads as translator indecision in teaching prose.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inversions, no swapped quantities, no dropped caveats (the 30-day trial, the billing-verification requirement and the "no se les cobrará" clause all survive intact), and the informal tú convention holds without a single slip ("Obtén", "Asegúrate", "Contáctanos", "Consulta", "Haz clic"). What a native technical editor would still change is a thin layer of translationese: "Nuestro equipo incluye expertos técnicos ... en toda esta gama de temas" is a word-for-word tracing of "Our team includes ... across this full range of topics" (native Spanish would be "cuenta con" / "sobre todos estos temas"); "hacer solicitudes de funciones" is a literal calque of "make feature requests" instead of the idiomatic "solicitar nuevas funciones"; and the English emphasis in "User will *not be charged*" is flattened to an unmarked "No se les cobrará", while "upgrade to other paid plans" is softened to the direction-neutral "cambiar a otros planes de pago". None of this misleads a learner; it just reads as competent MT in three spots.

examples.source: Our team includes technical experts ready to assist across this full range of topics.
examples.suggested: Nuestro equipo cuenta con expertos técnicos listos para ayudarte en todos estos temas.
examples.translation: Nuestro equipo incluye expertos técnicos listos para ayudarte en toda esta gama de temas.
examples.why: "incluye" + "en toda esta gama de temas" traces the English word for word; a Spanish technical writer would use "cuenta con" and drop the "range of topics" construction, which reads as a catalogue phrase in Spanish.

examples.source: To report bugs, make feature requests, and see what's coming in future releases
examples.suggested: Para reportar errores, solicitar nuevas funciones y ver lo que llegará en próximas versiones
examples.translation: Para reportar errores, hacer solicitudes de funciones y ver lo que viene en futuras versiones
examples.why: "hacer solicitudes de funciones" is a calque of "make feature requests"; the verb form "solicitar nuevas funciones" is the standard Spanish rendering in OSS docs. "lo que viene" is also flatter than "what's coming".

examples.source: User will *not be charged* if they continue using the free Open Plan, but can choose to upgrade to other paid plans at that time.
examples.suggested: *No se les cobrará* si siguen usando el Open Plan gratuito, aunque pueden optar por pasar a otros planes de pago en ese momento.
examples.translation: No se les cobrará si siguen usando el Open Plan gratuito, aunque pueden optar por cambiar a otros planes de pago en ese momento.
examples.why: The English italicises "not be charged" — the reassurance is the emphasized point of the sentence — and the emphasis is dropped. "upgrade" also becomes the direction-neutral "cambiar a", losing the sense of moving up to a higher plan.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inversions, no swapped quantities, no dropped caveats — and the informal "tu" holds with zero vous/votre/veuillez slips. The main defect is a within-file terminology split on "gate": the file mostly says "porte(s)" (~30 occurrences, e.g. "ensemble universel de portes quantiques", "portes de base") but leaks the capitalized English "Gate/Gates" at least ten times in prose — "le temps d'opération d'une Gate" (l.21), "plus de qubits et de gates CNOT" (l.207), "en Gates de base du dispositif" (l.364, in the same paragraph as "portes de base" at l.366), "de nombreuses Gates séquentielles" (l.369), "Gate sqrt(X), Gate X … Toute autre Gate" (l.381), "une **Gate de Toffoli (CCX)**" (l.383) immediately followed by "porte de Toffoli" in the l.384 heading, "une Gate complexe à 3 qubits" and "unitaire multi-Qubit" (l.418), and the summary bullet "**Gates Universelles**" (l.513). The same capitalized-anglicism pattern hits "Backend" ("un faux Backend" l.107/302 vs "sa version fictive" l.366) and "tout stack logiciel quantique" (l.418, for "any quantum software stack"), where a native writer would write "toute pile logicielle quantique". Remaining nits: the calque "à mesure que l'on évolue" / "au fur et à mesure que l'on évolue" (l.207, l.209) renders "as we scale up" as "as we evolve", "avec une probabilité de 100 % depuis la simulation" (l.253) calques "from the simulation" instead of "en simulation", and typography is inconsistent (French « » at l.41/212 vs straight "..." at l.300/362/421; "50 %" with space vs "2%" without at l.456).

examples.source: gate operation time / the device's basis gates / many sequential gates / a Toffoli (CCX) gate / Universal Gates
examples.suggested: le temps d'opération d'une porte / vers les portes de base du dispositif / de nombreuses portes séquentielles / une **porte de Toffoli (CCX)** / **Portes universelles**
examples.translation: le temps d'opération d'une Gate / en Gates de base du dispositif / de nombreuses Gates séquentielles / une **Gate de Toffoli (CCX)** / **Gates Universelles**
examples.why: The file's dominant and correct rendering is "porte"; the capitalized English "Gate/Gates" leaks ~10 times in prose, sometimes within the same paragraph as "portes de base" (l.364 vs l.366) and directly contradicting the adjacent heading "Décomposer une porte de Toffoli" (l.384). Recognizable, so not misleading, but a native technical editor would unify it.

examples.source: any multi-qubit unitary can be composed from 1- and 2-qubit gates. The transpiler is a crucial component of any quantum software stack
examples.suggested: n'importe quelle unitaire multi-qubit peut être composée à partir de portes à 1 et 2 qubits. Le transpileur est un composant crucial de toute pile logicielle quantique
examples.translation: n'importe quelle unitaire multi-Qubit peut être composée à partir de portes à 1 et 2 qubits. Le Transpiler est un composant crucial de tout stack logiciel quantique
examples.why: "multi-Qubit" capitalizes a common noun mid-word against the file's own lowercase "qubits", and "tout stack logiciel" is a raw anglicism with the wrong gender agreement for the French equivalent; "pile logicielle" (or at minimum "toute stack") is what a French quantum engineer would write.

examples.source: as we scale up, maintaining high fidelity gets harder without error correction / keeping those qubits well-behaved … as we scale
examples.suggested: à mesure que l'on monte en échelle, maintenir une haute fidélité devient plus difficile sans correction d'erreurs / … à mesure que l'on passe à l'échelle
examples.translation: à mesure que l'on évolue, maintenir une haute fidélité devient plus difficile sans correction d'erreurs / … au fur et à mesure que l'on évolue
examples.why: "que l'on évolue" reads as "as we evolve" — an intransitive use that has no scaling sense in French. The surrounding context (qubit count, circuit depth) rescues the meaning, so it is stiff translationese rather than misleading, but no native writer would phrase scaling this way.

examples.source: You should see `10` … with 100% probability from the simulation
examples.suggested: Tu devrais voir `10` … avec une probabilité de 100 % en simulation
examples.translation: Tu devrais voir `10` … avec une probabilité de 100 % depuis la simulation
examples.why: "depuis la simulation" is a word-for-word calque of English "from the simulation"; in French "depuis" is temporal/spatial and reads oddly here. "en simulation" or "dans la simulation" is the natural rendering.

examples.source: a fake backend that represents the IBM Quantum Brisbane device / a fake backend with known T1/T2 times / its fake version
examples.suggested: un **backend fictif** représentant l'appareil IBM Quantum Brisbane / un backend fictif avec des temps T1/T2 connus / sa version fictive
examples.translation: un **faux Backend** représentant l'appareil IBM Quantum Brisbane / un faux Backend avec des temps T1/T2 connus / sa version fictive
examples.why: Keeping "backend" in English is the defensible French convention, but capitalizing it mid-sentence is not, and the same concept ("fake backend") is split between "faux Backend" and "version fictive" a few paragraphs apart — the file already proves "fictive" is the better adjective.

editor_note: Faithful, idiomatic and consistently informal ("tu peux utiliser", "ton compte"); IBM/Cloud terminology is right and stable (platform logs → "journaux de plateforme" vs the distinct "journaux de services de plateforme", tenant kept as "tenant", "visualiser et recevoir des alertes sur", Required → "Obligatoire"), with no semantic drift in the two tables or the field descriptions.

Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, and the core math terms are right (וקטור עצמי / ערך עצמי for eigenvector/eigenvalue, זוגיות for parity, קבועה/מאוזנת for constant/balanced, בעיטת הפאזה for phase kickback used consistently). Two term problems a native editor would fix: "barriers" is rendered "מכסות" (= quotas/lids) instead of "מחסומים" — only the inline English gloss "(barriers)" saves it; and "in the exponent of $-1$" becomes "בחזקה של $-1$", which in Hebrew normally reads as raising something TO the power −1 rather than sitting IN the exponent of −1 (should be "במעריך של $-1$"). Several sentences are stiff calques: "ערך הפונקציה ... מבוצע עליו XOR על ה-Qubit התחתון" has a stray "עליו" that garbles the sentence, "תוך כדי זכירה שסקלרים עפים חופשי דרך מכפלות טנסוריות" and "המפתח שהופך את זה לעבוד" are word-for-word English syntax. The keep-English "Qubit"/"Hadamard" in Latin script is a defensible consistent convention, but the plural "מצבי ה-Qubitים" is an awkward one-off, and "not really a part of Deutsch's algorithm" drops the hedge ("אינו חלק"). None of this would make a learner form a false belief.

examples.source: Barriers are included to show the visual separation between the query gate implementation and the rest of the circuit.
examples.suggested: מחסומים (barriers) נוספו כדי להציג הפרדה חזותית בין מימוש שער השאילתה לשאר המעגל.
examples.translation: מכסות (barriers) כלולות כדי להציג הפרדה חזותית בין מימוש שער השאילתה לשאר המעגל.
examples.why: "מכסה/מכסות" means quota or lid; the Qiskit `barrier` is a מחסום. Recoverable only because the English word is glossed in parentheses, so it is imperfect-but-recognizable rather than misleading.

examples.source: Notice that in this expression, we have $f(0) \oplus f(1)$ in the exponent of $-1$ as opposed to $f(1) - f(0)$
examples.suggested: שימו לב שבביטוי זה $f(0) \oplus f(1)$ מופיע במעריך של $-1$ ולא $f(1) - f(0),$
examples.translation: שימו לב שבביטוי זה יש לנו $f(0) \oplus f(1)$ בחזקה של $-1$ ולא $f(1) - f(0),$
examples.why: "X בחזקה של Y" is the standard Hebrew for X^Y, so the sentence can be parsed as raising the XOR to the power −1. The intended term for "exponent" is מעריך (החזקה); the adjacent display math is what keeps it from actually misleading.

examples.source: the value of the function $f$ for the classical state of the top/rightmost qubit is XORed onto the bottom/leftmost qubit
examples.suggested: מבוצעת פעולת XOR בין ערך הפונקציה $f$ עבור המצב הקלסי של ה-Qubit העליון/הימני לבין ה-Qubit התחתון/השמאלי
examples.translation: ערך הפונקציה $f$ עבור המצב הקלסי של ה-Qubit העליון/הימני ביותר מבוצע עליו XOR על ה-Qubit התחתון/השמאלי ביותר
examples.why: The stray resumptive "עליו" plus the second "על" makes the clause read as if the XOR is applied to the function value itself; the target qubit is still identifiable, but no Hebrew technical writer would phrase it this way.

examples.source: Keeping in mind that scalars float freely through tensor products, we find an alternative way of reasoning how the operation $U_f$ transforms...
examples.suggested: אם נזכור שסקלרים עוברים בחופשיות דרך מכפלות טנסוריות, נקבל דרך חלופית להסביר כיצד הפעולה $U_f$ ממירה...
examples.translation: תוך כדי זכירה שסקלרים עפים חופשי דרך מכפלות טנסוריות, מוצאים דרך חלופית להסביר כיצד הפעולה $U_f$ ממירה...
examples.why: "תוך כדי זכירה" is a direct calque of "keeping in mind" and "עפים חופשי" is both ungrammatical (should be בחופשיות) and an odd metaphor in Hebrew; the English's light conversational tone flattens into robotic phrasing.

examples.source: we will trace through the action of the circuit above and identify the states of the qubits
examples.suggested: נעקוב אחר פעולת המעגל לעיל ונזהה את מצבי ה-Qubit
examples.translation: נעקוב אחר פעולת המעגל לעיל ונזהה את מצבי ה-Qubitים
examples.why: The file otherwise keeps the Latin-script "Qubit" uninflected ("ה-Qubit העליון", "וקטורי מצב Qubit"); the one-off Hebrew plural suffix glued to Latin letters ("Qubitים") is a within-file inconsistency and reads badly in RTL text.

editor_note: Nothing here misleads — every heading matches its English source semantically (the "4 qubit לכל תת-Circuit", the single wire cut + one `CRZGate`, the ancilla expansion, the 96 subexperiments are all faithful), and keeping Circuit/Gate/Backend/qubit/ancilla in English is a consistent, defensible glossary convention. What a native editor would still change: (1) the closing sentence "שלבים 3 ו-4 של [תבנית Qiskit] ניתן לבצע כפי שמוצג בהדרכות הקודמות" is syntactically broken Hebrew — a fronted object with an impersonal "ניתן" and no את; it should read "ניתן לבצע לאחר מכן את שלבים 3 ו-4…", and the English "can then" (temporal sequencing after the cutting steps) is dropped. (2) "sampling overhead" is rendered "עומס הדגימה" (= sampling load); the established Hebrew technical term for overhead is "תקורה", so "תקורת הדגימה" — recognizable but imprecise, and it also sits next to the untranslated "Sampling overhead:" in the output block. (3) Number/noun agreement and casing drift on the English-kept term: "4 qubit" (singular after a numeral) in the Step 2 heading vs capitalized "Qubit" in the ancilla heading, and "ancilla qubits" (plural) flattened to singular "ב-Qubit של ה-ancilla". (4) "מחיתוך ה-Gate-ים וחוטים אלה" drops the definite article on the second conjunct ("these gates and wires"), and the repeated image alt "תרשים Circuit קוונטי" is a word-order calque — a Hebrew writer would put the adjective with the noun ("תרשים מעגל קוונטי" or "תרשים Circuit"), not strand קוונטי after the Latin-script word.

examples.source: Steps 3 and 4 of a Qiskit pattern can then be performed as in the preceding tutorials.
examples.suggested: לאחר מכן ניתן לבצע את שלבים 3 ו-4 של [תבנית Qiskit] כפי שנעשה בהדרכות הקודמות.
examples.translation: שלבים 3 ו-4 של [תבנית Qiskit] ניתן לבצע כפי שמוצג בהדרכות הקודמות.
examples.why: Fronting the object before the impersonal ניתן without את is ungrammatical in Hebrew and reads as word-for-word English syntax; the sequencing sense of 'can then' is also lost.

examples.source: Calculate the sampling overhead incurred from cutting these gates and wires.
examples.suggested: חישוב תקורת הדגימה הנובעת מחיתוך ה-Gate-ים והחוטים הללו.
examples.translation: חישוב עומס הדגימה הנובע מחיתוך ה-Gate-ים וחוטים אלה.
examples.why: 'Overhead' is conventionally תקורה in Hebrew technical writing; עומס means load. Also 'וחוטים אלה' drops the definite article that 'these wires' requires alongside the definite ה-Gate-ים.

examples.source: a maximum of 4 qubits per subcircuit / expand the observables to account for ancilla qubits
examples.suggested: מקסימום של 4 qubits לכל תת-Circuit / כדי להתחשב ב-qubits של ה-ancilla
examples.translation: מקסימום של 4 qubit לכל תת-Circuit / כדי להתחשב ב-Qubit של ה-ancilla
examples.why: The kept-English term appears as singular 'qubit' after the numeral 4 and again as capitalized singular 'Qubit' for English plural 'ancilla qubits' — inconsistent casing and number for the same term within one file.

examples.source: Quantum circuit diagram (image alt text)
examples.suggested: תרשים Circuit / תרשים מעגל קוונטי
examples.translation: תרשים Circuit קוונטי
examples.why: Calqued English adjective order: קוונטי is stranded after the Latin-script noun, producing a mixed-script phrase no Hebrew technical writer would produce.

editor_note: Terminology is strong and consistent (gate/qubit/magic state/distiller/cat state kept in English; "toleran kesalahan", "blok kode", "kode permukaan"/"kode warna", "bobot", "generator stabilizer"), register is the plain "kita" convention with no deferential slips, and no claim is inverted or fabricated — so nothing misleads. What a native technical editor would change is pervasive translationese: English "suggests" (a figure indicating something) is rendered ~7 times as "menyarankan"/"disarankan" ("recommends/advises"), e.g. "seperti yang disarankan gambar berikut", "Gambar khusus ini ... menyarankan"; "introduce an error" is calqued three times as "memperkenalkan kesalahan" (introduce a person) instead of "menimbulkan/menyebabkan kesalahan". Two spots are locally garbled rather than merely stiff: "blok kode yang beroperasi di atasnya" reverses the agent of "the code block on which they operate", and "pemrosesan pasca-klasik" mis-parses "classical post-processing" into the nonsense "post-classical processing" (should be "pascapemrosesan klasik"). Smaller: "berisik" for a noisy CNOT clashes with the English "noise" used later in the same file; "koleksi magic state yang dikodekan dengan noise" reads "encoded with noise" rather than "noisy encoded"; and "Namun, memungkinkan untuk mengimplementasikan" (needs "dimungkinkan"), "ruang kode kode non-trivial", and the stray comma in "Ada juga, pendekatan alternatif" are grammar/flow slips.

examples.source: as the following figure suggests / consider the following figure, which suggests a transversal implementation of a CNOT gate
examples.suggested: seperti yang ditunjukkan gambar berikut / Pertimbangkan gambar berikut, yang menggambarkan implementasi transversal gate CNOT
examples.translation: seperti yang disarankan gambar berikut / Pertimbangkan gambar berikut, yang menyarankan implementasi transversal dari gate CNOT
examples.why: "menyarankan/disarankan" means "recommends/advises" in Indonesian; a figure does not advise. The calque of English "suggest" recurs ~7 times and is the single most conspicuous MT tell in the file.

examples.source: they can cause errors to propagate within the code block on which they operate
examples.suggested: dapat menyebabkan kesalahan menyebar di dalam blok kode tempat sirkuit tersebut beroperasi
examples.translation: dapat menyebabkan kesalahan menyebar di dalam blok kode yang beroperasi di atasnya
examples.why: The relative clause reverses the agent: "blok kode yang beroperasi di atasnya" says the code block operates on something else, when the circuits operate on the code block.

examples.source: it's a matter of measuring each physical qubit followed by classical post-processing
examples.suggested: cukup dengan mengukur setiap qubit fisik lalu melakukan pascapemrosesan klasik
examples.translation: itu adalah masalah mengukur setiap qubit fisik diikuti oleh pemrosesan pasca-klasik
examples.why: "pasca-" is attached to the wrong word, producing "post-classical processing" — a concept that does not exist — instead of "classical post-processing".

examples.source: any of these gates could fail and introduce an error / errors introduced by faulty gates
examples.suggested: bisa gagal dan menimbulkan kesalahan / kesalahan yang ditimbulkan oleh gate yang cacat
examples.translation: bisa gagal dan memperkenalkan kesalahan / kesalahan yang diperkenalkan oleh gate yang salah
examples.why: "memperkenalkan" is the social sense of "introduce" (introducing a person); Indonesian technical prose uses "menimbulkan/menyebabkan/memasukkan".

examples.source: a given controlled-NOT gate may itself be noisy / a collection of noisy encoded magic states
examples.suggested: gate controlled-NOT itu sendiri mungkin ber-noise / kumpulan magic state terkode yang ber-noise
examples.translation: gate controlled-NOT tertentu mungkin sendiri berisik / koleksi magic state yang dikodekan dengan noise
examples.why: "berisik" is acoustic loudness, and it is inconsistent with the English "noise" used later in the same file; "dikodekan dengan noise" additionally reads as "encoded with noise" rather than "noisy, encoded".

editor_note: Nothing here misleads a learner — every claim, caveat and quantity matches the English (the "pengguna Open Plan tidak dapat mengirimkan session job" caveat, "nilai ekspektasi", "setidaknya satu sirkuit"), and the informal "kamu" register holds throughout with no bapak/ibu slips. The main editorial defect is within-file inconsistency on "circuit": it appears as capitalized English "Circuit" in headings and prose ("Buat Circuit QASM", "Definisikan Circuit kuantum QASM", "mengurangi error pada Circuit") but as Indonesian "sirkuit" elsewhere ("setidaknya satu sirkuit"), and both forms collide inside a single sentence in the PUB admonition: "berisi satu sirkuit dan data yang disiarkan ke Circuit tersebut". The same stray mid-sentence capitalization hits "Backend" ("melihat Backend yang tersedia") and "Gate" ("tambahkan Gate terparameterisasi"), which reads like a glossary auto-replacement rather than an author's choice. Two smaller word-choice slips: "klasikal" for classical post-processing (Indonesian physics usage is "klasik"; "klasikal" reads as classroom-related), and "kebutuhan berikut" for the package "requirements" block, where a native technical writer would write "persyaratan"/"dependensi berikut".

examples.source: Each PUB is a tuple that contains one circuit and the data broadcasted to that circuit
examples.suggested: Setiap PUB adalah tuple yang berisi satu sirkuit dan data yang disebarkan ke sirkuit tersebut
examples.translation: Setiap PUB adalah tuple yang berisi satu sirkuit dan data yang disiarkan ke Circuit tersebut
examples.why: "circuit" is rendered two different ways inside one sentence (sirkuit / Circuit); pick one form file-wide. "disiarkan" is also a broadcast-media calque — "disebarkan"/"di-broadcast ke" fits the PUB data-broadcast sense better.

examples.source: Create a QASM circuit / Define a QASM quantum circuit / mitigate circuit errors
examples.suggested: Buat sirkuit QASM / Definisikan sirkuit kuantum QASM / mengurangi error pada sirkuit
examples.translation: Buat Circuit QASM / Definisikan Circuit kuantum QASM / mengurangi error pada Circuit
examples.why: Capitalized English "Circuit" (likewise "Backend" at line 41/282 and "Gate" at line 306) appears mid-sentence in running Indonesian prose. Indonesian does not capitalize common nouns; this reads as a glossary substitution artifact, not an author's decision to keep the term in English.

examples.source: classical post-processing overhead to mitigate errors in the raw results
examples.suggested: overhead pasca-pemrosesan klasik untuk mengurangi error pada hasil mentah
examples.translation: overhead pasca-pemrosesan klasikal untuk mengurangi error pada hasil mentah
examples.why: In Indonesian physics/computing usage the adjective is "klasik" (fisika klasik, komputasi klasik). "Klasikal" carries a classroom/group-instruction sense and is not the domain term.

examples.source: The code on this page was developed using the following requirements.
examples.suggested: Kode di halaman ini dikembangkan menggunakan persyaratan (dependensi) berikut.
examples.translation: Kode di halaman ini dikembangkan menggunakan kebutuhan berikut.
examples.why: "kebutuhan" is a literal gloss of "requirements" in the everyday "needs" sense; for a pinned-package list a native technical writer would write "persyaratan" or "dependensi". Understandable, but stiff.

editor_note: The dominant defect is a pervasive terminology leak around "circuit": the file renders it three different ways — correct "circuito/circuiti", an ungrammatical singular-with-plural-article "i circuito quantistici" / "i circuito graficamente" / "ottimizzare i circuito" / "i circuito vengono eseguiti", and a raw capitalized English "Circuit" left in Italian prose ("eseguire Circuit quantistici", "diagramma di Circuit", "il tuo Circuit Hello World", "un semplice Circuit a due qubit", "Funzione di supporto per l'esecuzione dei Circuit" — 10+ occurrences). The same leak pattern hits "l'instruction set del Backend" (capitalized English) and produces the coined verb "trascompilare" for "transpile" (conventional Italian keeps "transpilare"/"transpilazione"). Separately there are true calques a native technical writer would rewrite: "che entangles i due stati insieme" (English verb form conjugated inside Italian), "un Hadamard gate"/"un CNOT gate" in English word order while the same file later correctly writes "un gate $H$"/"un gate CX", "un'introduzione pratica e delicata" for "a gentle introduction", and "sistemi fisici che possono raccogliere rumore" for "pick up noise". One pedagogical flattening: the English "either outcome can happen when you measure" becomes "entrambi gli esiti possano verificarsi", which blunts the exact both-vs-either contrast that sentence exists to teach (the preceding clause still carries the caveat, so it does not actually mislead). Meaning is otherwise faithful throughout, the informal "tu" holds everywhere, and entanglement/sovrapposizione/shots/stato di Bell/qubit are correct and consistent.

examples.source: You'll learn about quantum circuits … simulators cannot run quantum circuits at the same scale … as our circuits become more complex
examples.suggested: Imparerai a conoscere i circuiti quantistici … non possono eseguire circuiti quantistici alla stessa scala … man mano che i nostri circuiti diventano più complessi
examples.translation: Imparerai a conoscere i circuito quantistici … non possono eseguire Circuit quantistici alla stessa scala … man mano che i nostri Circuit diventano più complessi
examples.why: The core term of the whole lesson is split three ways in one file: correct 'circuito/circuiti', an ungrammatical 'i circuito' (plural article + singular noun, repeated 4×), and an untranslated capitalized 'Circuit' left in Italian prose 10+ times, including a section heading ('Funzione di supporto per l'esecuzione dei Circuit') and 'diagramma di Circuit'. Looks like a glossary/leak-fixer artifact rather than a translator choice.

examples.source: Then we apply a $CX$ (controlled-NOT) gate, which entangles the two states together.
examples.suggested: Poi applichiamo un gate $CX$ (controlled-NOT), che mette in entanglement i due qubit.
examples.translation: Poi applichiamo un gate $CX$ (controlled-NOT), che entangles i due stati insieme.
examples.why: 'che entangles' leaves an English third-person verb form inside Italian syntax — no native technical writer would write this; 'insieme' is a further calque of 'together'. The file already uses the noun 'entanglement' correctly elsewhere, so the verb should follow the same convention ('mette in entanglement').

examples.source: This function takes care of transpiling the circuit to match the backend's instruction set
examples.suggested: Questa funzione si occupa di transpilare il circuito per adattarlo al set di istruzioni del backend
examples.translation: Questa funzione si occupa di trascompilare il circuito per adattarlo all'instruction set del Backend
examples.why: 'trascompilare' is a coined verb; the Italian Qiskit community says 'transpilare'/'transpilazione'. 'l'instruction set del Backend' mixes an untranslated English compound with a capitalized 'Backend' — 'set di istruzioni del backend' is the conventional rendering, and 'backend' is lowercase everywhere else in the file's code.

examples.source: Superposition doesn't mean you'll ever see both results in one measurement; it means the state is set up so that either outcome can happen when you measure.
examples.suggested: …significa che lo stato è predisposto in modo che, quando misuri, possa verificarsi l'uno o l'altro esito.
examples.translation: La sovrapposizione non significa che vedrai mai entrambi i risultati in una singola misurazione; significa che lo stato è configurato in modo che entrambi gli esiti possano verificarsi quando misuri.
examples.why: The English pivots deliberately on 'both' (negated) vs 'either' (affirmed) — that contrast IS the misconception being corrected. Rendering both halves with 'entrambi' flattens the distinction and makes the sentence read as self-contradictory; 'l'uno o l'altro esito' restores the teaching point.

examples.source: a gentle, hands-on introduction … the red box labeled "H" is a Hadamard gate … a CNOT gate … physical systems that can pick up noise
examples.suggested: un'introduzione pratica e graduale … è un gate di Hadamard … un gate CNOT … sistemi fisici soggetti a rumore
examples.translation: un'introduzione pratica e delicata … il riquadro rosso etichettato "H" è un Hadamard gate … un CNOT gate … sistemi fisici che possono raccogliere rumore
examples.why: 'delicata' means fragile/sensitive, not 'gentle' in the pedagogical sense ('graduale'/'soft'). 'un Hadamard gate'/'un CNOT gate' keep English noun-noun order, and the same file later writes the correct Italian order ('un gate $H$', 'un gate CX'), so it is inconsistent as well as calqued. 'raccogliere rumore' is a literal rendering of 'pick up noise'.

editor_note: No semantic drift: every claim, condition and caveat matches the English (Pauli-Lindblad vs TREX selection by gate/measurement content, client-side vs server-side split, "non prende decisioni implicite per te" all faithful), and core terminology is correct and consistent — "valori di aspettazione", "gate a uno e due qubit", "mitigazione degli errori", with box/samplex/template circuit/twirling/pass correctly kept in English throughout; informal "tu" holds everywhere (Sei invitato, puoi, consulta, Dai un'occhiata). What a native editor would change is a handful of calques and stiff constructions: "Sentiti libero di inviare feedback" is a word-for-word "feel free" (Italian uses "Non esitare a"); "strati unici" for "unique layers" is ambiguous (reads as "the only layers") where "strati distinti/univoci" is meant, and it recurs twice; "trattate come aventi un contesto di rumore stabile" and the parenthetical "(tranne che con diversi valori dei parametri assegnati)" are bureaucratic/garbled-sounding where the English is plain. Also "nell'attuale Sampler ed Estimator" should agree in the plural ("negli attuali"), and "reproduce results" was nominalized into "la riproducibilità dei risultati", shifting the emphasis from an action the reader performs to an abstract property.

examples.source: Feel free to submit feedback and report bugs in its GitHub repository.
examples.suggested: Non esitare a inviare feedback e a segnalare bug nel repository GitHub del progetto.
examples.translation: Sentiti libero di inviare feedback e segnalare bug nel suo repository GitHub.
examples.why: "Sentiti libero" is a direct calque of "feel free" that Italian technical writing avoids; the idiomatic invitation is "Non esitare a".

examples.source: Learn the noise models of the unique layers … returns the noise model for each unique layer.
examples.suggested: …degli strati distinti … per ogni strato distinto (o "univoco").
examples.translation: Apprendi i modelli di rumore degli strati unici … restituisce il modello di rumore per ogni strato unico.
examples.why: "unique" here means "distinct/non-repeated", but Italian "unico" primarily reads as "the only one", blurring the stratification concept; "distinto"/"univoco" is the conventional rendering.

examples.source: …collections of circuit operations that should be treated as having a stable noise context
examples.suggested: …insiemi di operazioni del circuito da trattare come se condividessero un contesto di rumore stabile
examples.translation: …insiemi di operazioni del circuito che devono essere trattate come aventi un contesto di rumore stabile
examples.why: The present-participle "come aventi" is legalese-stiff; a native technical writer would use a subordinate clause, and the plain English deserves plain Italian.

examples.source: …a parameterized circuit that will be executed without further alteration (other than having different parameter values assigned to it).
examples.suggested: …senza ulteriori modifiche (se non per l'assegnazione di valori diversi ai parametri).
examples.translation: …un circuito parametrizzato che verrà eseguito senza ulteriori modifiche (tranne che con diversi valori dei parametri assegnati).
examples.why: The parenthetical is syntactically broken Italian — "tranne che con" does not govern the noun phrase — and the reader has to reconstruct the intended exception.

examples.source: …techniques that are built into the existing Sampler and Estimator
examples.suggested: …le tecniche integrate negli attuali Sampler ed Estimator
examples.translation: …le tecniche integrate nell'attuale Sampler ed Estimator
examples.why: Singular "nell'attuale" governing two coordinated nouns is an agreement slip that a native editor would fix on sight.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the gate-by-gate construction (qubit 0 に Hadamard、qubit 0 を制御・qubit 1 をターゲットとする CNOT、qubit 2 に X), the VQC/特徴マップ paragraph, and the closing 変分形式/アンザッツ sentence all match the English exactly, register is clean desu/masu with no keigo, and 重ね合わせ・エンタングルメント・アンザッツ are the right domain terms. The real problem is the keep-English glossary being over-applied to "circuit" and "gate": the file writes 「テンプレート Circuit」「パラメータ化された Circuit」「Circuit 図」and 「X Gate」「Hadamard Gate」「CNOT (CX) Gate」in bare Latin script mid-sentence, where a Japanese quantum engineer writes 回路 / 回路図 / ゲート — 「Circuit 図」for "circuit diagram" is especially un-Japanese. It is also inconsistent within the file: "circuit" is 量子回路 at lines 17 and 19 but Circuit at lines 62, 64, 84 and 109. Two smaller nuance flattenings: the italicized conditional "*if* we bind the parameters" becomes the means-clause 「パラメータをバインドする*ことで*」 (line 64), losing the "only under this condition" force that 「〜すれば」would keep, and "an educated guess" is reduced to plain 「推測値」 (line 17), dropping the "educated"/根拠のある sense.

examples.source: template circuits / parameterized circuit / A circuit diagram of a unitary operator
examples.suggested: テンプレート回路 / パラメータ化された回路 / ユニタリ演算子の回路図
examples.translation: テンプレート Circuit / パラメータ化された Circuit / 参照状態を準備するユニタリ演算子の Circuit 図 — but 量子回路 at lines 17, 19
examples.why: "circuit" is rendered two ways within one file: 回路 inside 量子回路 but bare English "Circuit" everywhere else. 「Circuit 図」 is a hybrid no native technical writer would produce — 回路図 is the settled term. Recognizable, so not misleading, but a native editor would unify on 回路.

examples.source: apply an X gate to qubit 0 … a Hadamard gate on qubit 0 … a CNOT (CX) gate
examples.suggested: qubit $0$ に X ゲートを適用する … アダマールゲート（$H_0$）… CNOT (CX) ゲート（$CNOT_{01}$）
examples.translation: qubit $0$ に X Gate を適用する … qubit $0$ に Hadamard Gate（$H_0$）を適用し … CNOT (CX) Gate（$CNOT_{01}$）
examples.why: Capitalized English "Gate" embedded in Japanese prose reads as untranslated source text. ゲート (katakana) is the universal convention in Japanese Qiskit/quantum writing; keeping qubit in English is defensible, keeping Gate is not.

examples.source: but we can use them for our reference states *if* we bind the parameters
examples.suggested: パラメータをバインド*すれば*参照状態に使用できます
examples.translation: パラメータをバインドする*ことで*参照状態に使用することができます
examples.why: The English italicizes *if* to stress that binding is the precondition for reusing a template circuit as a reference state. 「ことで」turns the condition into a means ("by binding"), and the emphasis markers land on a grammatical particle, so the pedagogical point that unbound parameters disqualify the circuit is softened.

examples.source: If you have an educated guess or datapoint from an existing optimal solution
examples.suggested: 根拠のある推測や、既存の最適解から得られたデータ点がある場合
examples.translation: 既存の最適解から得られた推測値やデータ点がある場合
examples.why: "educated guess" is flattened to plain 推測値 (a guessed value), dropping the "informed/well-founded" sense that motivates why it speeds convergence. The JA also binds 既存の最適解から得られた to both nouns, whereas in the English the qualifier attaches most naturally only to "datapoint". Nuance loss, not a false statement.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the Estimator/Pauli-decomposition derivation, the sparse-vs-dense efficiency argument, the bias/variance trade-off, and the max-cut z_i = 1-2x_i mapping all match the English exactly, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The file does, however, split into two terminological halves: "circuit" is left as English "Circuit" through the Primitives/Error-Suppression sections (양자 Circuit, 보조 Circuit, 유휴 Qubit) but becomes "회로" from Error Mitigation onward (회로 오류, 회로당 샷 수, 노이즈 증폭된 모든 회로); likewise "primitives" is "primitives"/"Primitive" early and "프리미티브" late (lines 785, 791, 939), "Pauli" alternates 파울리 연산자 (l.64-81) vs Pauli 연산자 / Pauli $Z$ (l.496, 529), and "qubit" alternates Qubit/qubit within the same paragraph area (l.43 vs l.47, l.674 vs l.726). Two smaller items: the opening bullet renders "optimize speed versus accuracy" as "속도와 정확도를 최적화하는", which reads as optimizing both rather than trading them off (the Summary at l.940 gets it right with "속도 대 정확도"), and one sentence at l.712 drops into 해요체 ("살펴봐요") amid an otherwise uniform 합니다체 document. Several image alt texts (l.789, 805, 821, 932, 944) also remain untranslated English while others were translated.

examples.source: a quantum circuit that prepares the state |ψ⟩ … reduce circuit errors by modeling the device noise
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering for the whole file — either 회로 everywhere or Circuit everywhere (the same split hits 보조 Circuit/노이즈 증폭된 모든 회로, 유휴 Qubit/qubit 연결성).
examples.translation: 상태 $|\psi\rangle$를 준비하는 양자 Circuit … 회로 오류를 줄이는 기법
examples.why: The first half of the lesson keeps 'Circuit' in English while the error-mitigation half switches to 회로; the concept stays identifiable, but a native editor would unify it.

examples.source: Qiskit offers two primitives … Primitives allow for the use of error suppression techniques … The Qiskit Runtime primitive's resilience_level option
examples.suggested: Use one form consistently — either the English 'primitives' (as in the section headings) or 프리미티브 throughout.
examples.translation: 두 가지 primitives가 도움이 됩니다 … Primitive는 `optimization_level` 옵션을 … Qiskit Runtime 프리미티브의 `resilience_level` 옵션
examples.why: Three renderings of the same core term (primitives / Primitive / 프리미티브) inside one file; same pattern for 파울리 vs Pauli.

examples.source: Defining a measurement strategy with the Qiskit Runtime primitives to optimize speed versus accuracy
examples.suggested: Qiskit Runtime primitives를 사용하여 속도 대 정확도의 균형을 조정하는 측정 전략 정의
examples.translation: Qiskit Runtime primitives를 사용하여 속도와 정확도를 최적화하는 측정 전략 정의
examples.why: '속도와 정확도를 최적화' reads as optimizing both at once and loses the trade-off that the whole 'Measurement strategy: speed versus accuracy' section is built on; the Summary bullet (l.940) already uses the correct '속도 대 정확도'.

examples.source: We can use a simulator to show the usefulness of an optimized transpilation.
examples.suggested: 시뮬레이터를 활용해 최적화된 트랜스파일의 유용성을 살펴보겠습니다.
examples.translation: 시뮬레이터를 활용해 최적화된 트랜스파일의 유용성을 살펴봐요.
examples.why: Single 해요체 sentence in a file that is otherwise uniformly 합니다체 (e.g. the neighbouring l.710 '…살펴봐요' vs l.680 '…확인해 보겠습니다'); the abrupt speech-level switch is jarring to a Korean reader.

examples.source: This is a very simple circuit used as a toy model.
examples.suggested: 이는 예시용 토이 모델로 사용한 매우 단순한 회로입니다.
examples.translation: 이는 장난감 모델로 사용된 매우 단순한 Circuit입니다.
examples.why: '장난감 모델' is a literal calque; Korean physics/quantum writing normally says 토이 모델 or 단순화된 모형, and the sentence also mixes the calque with the English 'Circuit'.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inversions, dropped caveats or hallucinated claims — but a native technical editor would change several things. The four-step bullet list is half-untranslated: "**실행**: 대상 하드웨어에서 Execute" and "**후처리**: 결과 Post-process" leave the English verbs stranded inside Korean sentences (ungrammatical), and they contradict the section headings that do translate them (실행하기 / 결과 후처리하기). Core nouns are kept in English with inconsistent casing — "양자 Circuit", "추상 Circuit", "ISA Circuit" (never 회로), "Qubit"(l.24) vs "qubit"(ll.30, 32, 42), "기본 Gate"/"다중 qubit Gate" — where Korean quantum docs conventionally write 회로/큐비트/게이트. Two domain renderings are imperfect: "postselection" becomes "후처리 선택", which collides with 후처리 (post-processing) in the very same section instead of the standard 후선택, and "per-shot measurements" becomes "측정별(per-shot) 값" rather than 샷별 측정값. "transpiled" is paraphrased as "Transpiler를 통해 변환"/"병렬 Transpiler 처리" instead of 트랜스파일. Register is uniform 합니다체 (standard and defensible for Korean docs), with no honorific/humble slips; 기댓값, 관측량, 커플링 맵, 준확률 분포 are all correct and consistent.

examples.source:
- **Execute** on target hardware
- **Post-process** results
examples.suggested:
- **실행**: 대상 하드웨어에서 실행
- **후처리**: 결과 후처리
examples.translation:
- **실행**: 대상 하드웨어에서 Execute
- **후처리**: 결과 Post-process
examples.why: Glossary leak: the English verbs are left untranslated mid-sentence, producing ungrammatical Korean, and they clash with the section headings (실행하기 / 결과 후처리하기) that do render them in Korean. The other two bullets (매핑/최적화) are fully translated, so the list is internally inconsistent.

examples.source: or postselection on inherent properties of the problem, such as total spin, parity, or particle conservation
examples.suggested: 또는 ... 문제의 고유 특성에 대한 후선택(postselection)
examples.translation: 또는 총 스핀, 패리티, ... 입자 보존과 같은 문제의 고유 특성에 따른 후처리 선택
examples.why: Postselection is conventionally 후선택. Rendering it 후처리 선택 inside the '결과 후처리하기' section reads as 'choosing a post-processing step' rather than 'discarding runs that violate a constraint' — recognizable from context, but the wrong technique name.

examples.source: If using Sampler, the output will be per-shot measurements in the form of bitstrings.
examples.suggested: Sampler를 사용하면 출력은 비트열 형태의 샷별 측정 결과가 됩니다.
examples.translation: Sampler를 사용하는 경우 출력은 비트 문자열 형태의 측정별(per-shot) 값이 됩니다.
examples.why: 'per-shot' is glossed as 측정별 ('per measurement'), swapping which noun is the unit: the shot is the unit and the measurement is the thing counted. The parenthetical (per-shot) rescues the reader, but the Korean noun phrase itself is wrong.

examples.source: abstract circuits must be transpiled to Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) circuits / allows parallel transpilation
examples.suggested: 추상 회로를 ISA 회로로 트랜스파일해야 합니다 / 병렬 트랜스파일
examples.translation: 추상 Circuit을 명령어 집합 아키텍처(ISA) Circuit으로 Transpiler를 통해 변환해야 합니다 / 병렬 Transpiler 처리
examples.why: The verb 'transpile' is paraphrased as 'convert via the Transpiler', and 'transpilation' becomes '병렬 Transpiler 처리' — a Korean quantum engineer writes 트랜스파일/트랜스파일링. Naming the tool where the process is meant is stiff and reads as machine output.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inversion, no swapped quantity, no dropped caveat; the ansatz/variational-form definition, the $D = 2^{2n}$ dimensionality passage, the "at least one layer must contain parameters" bullet and the max-cut/QAOA setup all land correctly, and "nilai jangkaan" (expectation value), "Hamiltonian Pauli", "keadaan rujukan" and "fungsi kos" are correct and consistent. The defects are terminology-consistency and polish. "circuit" is rendered "litar" ~20 times but leaks untranslated as capitalised "Circuit" three times ("sebagai Circuit pengelasan", "Circuit `QAOAAnsatz` dari perpustakaan Circuit Qiskit", line ~153/191), and "qubit" alternates between lowercase "qubit" and mid-word capital "Qubit" ("sistem $n$-Qubit", "qubit-Qubit", "lima-Qubit", "satu-Qubit", "$2$-Qubit") — both read as glossary-fixer artefacts. "trade-off" is rendered two ways: "pertukaran" (= exchange/swap, weak and slightly misreadable in "terdapat beberapa pertukaran yang perlu dipertimbangkan") in the heading and bullets, but the idiomatic "mengimbangi antara kelajuan dan ketepatan" in the intro and summary. Smaller items: the calque "Ia mungkin untuk mencipta litar berparameter ini…" for "It is possible to create…", "dua uniti" for "two unitaries" (should be "unitari") in the summary alt text, "mencipta contoh `Parameter`" for "creating a `Parameter` instance", the typo "pengekodkan" for "pengekodan", and casual "kamu" at lines ~88/94/241 where the file's convention is "anda"/"kita".

examples.source: or as a classification circuit for machine learning … by using the `QAOAAnsatz` circuit from the Qiskit circuit library
examples.suggested: atau sebagai litar pengelasan untuk pembelajaran mesin … menggunakan litar `QAOAAnsatz` daripada pustaka litar Qiskit
examples.translation: atau sebagai Circuit pengelasan untuk pembelajaran mesin … menggunakan Circuit `QAOAAnsatz` dari perpustakaan Circuit Qiskit
examples.why: 'circuit' is translated 'litar' everywhere else in the file; three capitalised English 'Circuit' leaks break the file's own convention (and 'perpustakaan' is the book-library sense — computing Malay uses 'pustaka').

examples.source: An $n$-qubit system … correlations between the qubits … a five-qubit `NLocal` circuit … single-qubit rotation gates and $2$-qubit entanglement gates
examples.suggested: Sistem $n$-qubit … korelasi penting antara qubit … litar `NLocal` lima qubit … gate putaran satu qubit dan gate keterikatan $2$ qubit
examples.translation: Sistem $n$-Qubit … korelasi penting antara qubit-Qubit … litar `NLocal` lima-Qubit … gate putaran satu-Qubit dan gate keterikatan $2$-Qubit
examples.why: 'qubit' is capitalised mid-compound in some places and lowercase in others within the same file; 'qubit-Qubit' is also a malformed reduplication that no Malay technical writer would produce.

examples.source: Heuristic ansaetze and trade-offs … there are some trade-offs to consider … There is a fundamental trade-off between quality … and speed
examples.suggested: Heuristic ansaetze dan tolak ansur … terdapat beberapa tolak ansur yang perlu dipertimbangkan … Terdapat tolak ansur asas antara kualiti … dan kelajuan
examples.translation: Heuristic ansaetze dan pertukaran … terdapat beberapa pertukaran yang perlu dipertimbangkan … Terdapat pertukaran asas antara kualiti … dan kelajuan
examples.why: 'pertukaran' means exchange/swap, not trade-off, and the same concept is rendered idiomatically as 'mengimbangi antara kelajuan dan ketepatan' at lines 21 and 244 — imperfect term plus within-file split.

examples.source: It is possible to create this parametrized circuit without binding specific angles yet:
examples.suggested: Litar berparameter ini boleh dicipta tanpa mengikat sudut tertentu terlebih dahulu:
examples.translation: Ia mungkin untuk mencipta litar berparameter ini tanpa mengikat sudut tertentu dahulu:
examples.why: 'Ia mungkin untuk…' is a word-for-word calque of the English dummy-subject 'It is possible to…'; Malay technical prose uses a 'boleh' passive instead.

examples.source: A circuit diagram showing two unitaries: one preparing the reference state and another preparing the ansatz.
examples.suggested: Gambar rajah litar menunjukkan dua operator unitari: satu menyediakan keadaan rujukan dan satu lagi menyediakan ansatz.
examples.translation: Gambar rajah litar menunjukkan dua uniti: satu menyediakan keadaan rujukan dan satu lagi menyediakan ansatz.
examples.why: 'uniti' is 'unit/unity', not 'unitary' — the correct Malay term for a unitary operator is 'unitari'.

examples.source: If you do not have any information about your particular problem … the more likely you are to find a precise result … you learned how to define your search space
examples.suggested: Jika anda tidak mempunyai … lebih besar kemungkinan anda akan menemui … anda telah belajar cara mentakrifkan ruang carian anda
examples.translation: Jika kamu tidak mempunyai sebarang maklumat tentang masalah tertentu … lebih besar kemungkinan kamu akan menemui hasil yang tepat … kamu telah belajar cara mentakrifkan ruang carian kamu
examples.why: Casual 'kamu' in three places where the file's own convention (and the locale standard for instructional prose) is 'anda'/'kita'.

editor_note: The large-scale section inverts the load-bearing concept: "as many disjoint Bell pairs as its connectivity allows" is rendered "أزواج Bell المتقاطعة" — *intersecting/overlapping* pairs, the exact opposite of disjoint, in the one sentence that explains why the CHSH test scales (the code beside it explicitly builds edges that "share no qubits"). A learner would form the false belief that the tiling deliberately overlaps qubits. A second drift strengthens a claim in the Background: "is used to experimentally test Bell's theorem" becomes "تُستخدم لإثبات نظرية Bell تجريبياً" (*to prove*), turning a falsifiable experimental test into a proof. Beyond those: "coupling map" is split between خريطة الاتصال (simulator paragraph) and خريطة الاقتران (tiling paragraph); "transpile" is rendered once as ننقل الدوائر ("we move the circuits") and once as الدائرة المُحوَّلة; "raw counts" becomes العدادات الخام ("raw counters" rather than measurement counts); and "Wherever a curve enters the grey bands" reads as an idafa — "يدخل فيه منحنى النطاقات الرمادية" parses as "the curve of the grey bands enters". Register is consistently informal (تأكد، اخترته، إذا وجدت) and قيم التوقع / رواصد / شواهد are used correctly and consistently.

examples.source: Here we tile the backend with as many disjoint Bell pairs as its connectivity allows (a *matching* of the coupling map) and run an independent CHSH sub-circuit on every pair
examples.suggested: هنا نُغطّي الـ Backend بأكبر عدد ممكن من أزواج Bell غير المتقاطعة (المنفصلة) الذي تسمح به التوصيلية (مطابقة لخريطة الاقتران)…
examples.translation: هنا نُبلّط الـ Backend بأكبر عدد ممكن من أزواج Bell المتقاطعة تسمح به التوصيلية (مطابقة خريطة الاقتران) ونُشغّل دائرة CHSH فرعية مستقلة على كل زوج
examples.why: ‘disjoint’ → ‘المتقاطعة’ means *intersecting/overlapping* — the inverse of the source. The entire scaling argument rests on pairs that share no qubits (the accompanying code comment says exactly that), so the learner is taught the opposite of the mechanism.

examples.source: The CHSH inequality, named after Clauser, Horne, Shimony, and Holt, is used to experimentally test Bell's theorem (1969).
examples.suggested: …تُستخدم لاختبار نظرية Bell تجريبياً (1969).
examples.translation: متباينة CHSH، المسماة نسبةً إلى مؤلفيها Clauser وHorne وShimony وHolt، تُستخدم لإثبات نظرية Bell تجريبياً (1969).
examples.why: ‘test’ is strengthened to ‘إثبات’ (prove). The next sentence already uses إثبات for what a *violation* demonstrates, so the distinction between testing a theorem and proving it is lost — a real conceptual point in this tutorial.

examples.source: the noise model and coupling map of the backend you selected … (a *matching* of the coupling map)
examples.suggested: استخدم خريطة الاقتران في الموضعين
examples.translation: نموذج الضوضاء وخريطة الاتصال للـ Backend الذي اخترته … (مطابقة خريطة الاقتران)
examples.why: ‘coupling map’ is rendered two different ways in the same file; a reader can’t tell the simulator’s ‘خريطة الاتصال’ is the same object as the device’s ‘خريطة الاقتران’ used for the tiling.

examples.source: transpile against the simulator's target … the transpiled circuit's qubit layout
examples.suggested: ونُترجم (نُحوّل) الدوائر وفقاً لهدف المحاكٍ … تخطيط الـ Qubit للدائرة المُترجَمة
examples.translation: وننقل الدوائر وفقاً لهدف المحاكٍ … تخطيط الـ Qubit للدائرة المُحوَّلة
examples.why: ‘transpile’ as ‘ننقل’ reads as ‘we move/transfer the circuits’, which is not what the pass manager does, and it does not match ‘المُحوَّلة’ used three paragraphs later for the same operation.

examples.source: we obtain the expectation values … directly, without reconstructing them from raw counts
examples.suggested: … دون الحاجة إلى استنتاجها من أعداد النتائج الخام (الإحصاءات الخام)
examples.translation: نحصل مباشرةً على قيم التوقع … دون الحاجة إلى استنتاجها من العدادات الخام
examples.why: ‘counts’ (measurement outcome tallies) is rendered ‘العدادات’ = counters/meters, an object rather than the data; it obscures the Estimator-vs-Sampler contrast the sentence is making.

examples.source: Wherever a curve enters the grey bands, it has crossed the classical bound of ±2
examples.suggested: وكلّما دخل أحد المنحنيات النطاقاتِ الرمادية، يكون قد تجاوز الحد الكلاسيكي $\pm 2$
examples.translation: في أي مكان يدخل فيه منحنى النطاقات الرمادية، يكون قد تجاوز الحد الكلاسيكي $\pm 2$
examples.why: ‘منحنى النطاقات الرمادية’ parses as an idafa — ‘the curve of the grey bands’ — so the sentence momentarily says the wrong thing; a native technical writer would mark the object or restructure with كلّما.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the tricky precedence sentence ("إذا حُدِّد خيار أثناء تهيئة الـ primitive وبعدها، فإن القيمة المُضبَطة بعد تهيئة الـ primitive هي التي تُستخدَم") and the whole feature-compatibility matrix are correct, and the informal register (انقر، راجع، يمكنك) holds. The defects are terminological, not misleading: "shot" is rendered "تشغيل" (a run) in `execution.init_qubits`, which blurs the per-shot vs per-job distinction that is the whole point of that option — "لقطة" (or keeping "shot") is the field convention. "instance" and "copy" are both rendered "نسخة" in the Primitive-initialization paragraph, so "pass in an instance … which then makes a copy" collapses into "نسخة … نسخة" (Arabic convention is "مثيل" for instance); "dynamical decoupling" is "الفصل الديناميكي" rather than the conventional "فك الاقتران الديناميكي"; and "method" is calqued as "الطريقة" ("استخدم الطريقة `update()`") where a native technical writer would write "التابع"/"الدالة".

examples.source: Whether to reset the qubits to the ground state for each shot.
examples.suggested: … إلى الحالة الأرضية عند كل لقطة (shot).
examples.translation: ما إذا كان سيتم إعادة تعيين الـ Qubits إلى الحالة الأرضية لكل تشغيل.
examples.why: "shot" is rendered as "تشغيل" (a run/execution), the same word an Arabic reader uses for running a job. It blurs the per-shot granularity that init_qubits is about; "لقطة" (or keeping "shot") is the established rendering. Imperfect but still recognizable, hence minor.

examples.source: You can pass in an instance of the options class or a dictionary when initializing Executor, which then makes a copy of those options.
examples.suggested: يمكنك تمرير مثيل من فئة الخيارات أو قاموسًا عند تهيئة Executor، فيُنشئ عندئذٍ نسخة من تلك الخيارات.
examples.translation: يمكنك تمرير نسخة من فئة الخيارات أو قاموس عند تهيئة Executor، والذي يُنشئ بعد ذلك نسخة من تلك الخيارات.
examples.why: "instance" and "copy" are both "نسخة", so the sentence reads "a copy … which makes a copy" and the object-vs-duplicate contrast that motivates the next sentence is flattened. "مثيل" is the standard Arabic term for a class instance.

examples.source: Dynamical decoupling
examples.suggested: فك الاقتران الديناميكي
examples.translation: الفصل الديناميكي
examples.why: "الفصل" means separation/splitting; decoupling in this technique is undoing a coupling to the environment, conventionally "فك الاقتران". Recognizable in context (it sits next to ZNE/PEA/PEC), so minor, but not the field term.

examples.source: Use the `update()` method to apply changes to the `options` attribute. … You can use the built-in `asdict` method …
examples.suggested: استخدم التابع `update()` لتطبيق التغييرات على الخاصية `options`. … يمكنك استخدام التابع المُضمَّن `asdict` …
examples.translation: استخدم الطريقة `update()` لتطبيق التغييرات على خاصية `options`. … يمكنك استخدام الطريقة المضمَّنة `asdict` …
examples.why: "الطريقة" is a literal calque of "method"; Arabic technical prose uses "التابع" (or "الدالة"). Placing it before the code identifier ("الطريقة `update()`") also reads like translated English rather than native documentation.

editor_note: Nothing here misleads a learner — meaning, quantities (~16 mH, 1.6 mH, first five orbitals) and caveats ("kvantové vzorky v této ukázce byly čistý šum") all survive, and the informal register is consistent (nahraď, najdeš, Vyber, Spusť, Pamatuj). But an editor would change several things. The biggest is an untranslated-glossary leak with within-file inconsistency: "circuit" appears both as normal Czech "obvod" and as capitalized English "Circuit" — in adjacent sentences on line 159 ("optimalizujeme náš obvod… Před optimalizací Circuit musíme zvolit"), plus "kvantový Circuit", "Circuit je vzorkován", "falešný Backend", "interakce Qubitů"/"fyzické Qubity" (yet lowercase "36-qubitového"), "Transpileru", "režim spuštění Job", "Pattern lze popsat". Second, two domain renderings are off-convention: "sebekonsistentní" throughout where Czech chemistry/physics says "samokonzistentní", and "keyword arguments" → "klíčové argumenty" (reads as "crucial arguments", not named/keyword arguments). Third, translationese: the coined verb "post-procesovat"/"Post-procesování" for post-process, the mathematical "supported in a set of basis states" rendered as "vlnová funkce je podpořena sadou bázových stavů" (endorsed, not "má nosič v"), "operátory tvorby/anihilace" for the standard "kreační a anihilační operátory", and "dvou-tělesové elektronové integrály" for "dvouelektronové integrály". One line is also grammatically broken: "mají orbitaly různých spinů propojení každý 4. orbital" is missing the preposition.

examples.source: Next, we will optimize our circuit for a target hardware. We need to choose the hardware device to use before optimizing our circuit.
examples.suggested: Dále optimalizujeme náš obvod pro cílový hardware. Před optimalizací obvodu musíme zvolit hardwarové zařízení.
examples.translation: Dále optimalizujeme náš obvod pro cílový hardware. Před optimalizací Circuit musíme zvolit hardwarové zařízení.
examples.why: "circuit" is rendered both as the correct Czech "obvod" and as an untranslated capitalized "Circuit" — here in two adjacent sentences, and likewise at lines 53, 54, 56, 110, 172, 204. The same leak hits "Backend" (l. 20, 159), "Qubitů/Qubity" (l. 125, 169) against lowercase "36-qubitového" (l. 13), "Transpileru" (l. 171) and "Job" (l. 202). Reads as an unfinished glossary pass, not as a Czech engineer's prose.

examples.source: The example below also shows how to pass keyword arguments to that function via the included solver.
examples.suggested: … jak této funkci předat pojmenované (keyword) argumenty prostřednictvím zahrnutého solveru.
examples.translation: Níže uvedený příklad také ukazuje, jak předat klíčové argumenty této funkci prostřednictvím zahrnutého solveru.
examples.why: "klíčové argumenty" means "crucial/key arguments", not Python keyword arguments. Recoverable from the `max_cycle=200` example that follows, so not misleading, but it is the wrong term for a Python concept.

examples.source: the wave function is supported in a set of basis states $\mathcal{S}$ whose size does not increase exponentially
examples.suggested: vlnová funkce má nosič v množině bázových stavů $\mathcal{S}$, jejíž velikost neroste exponenciálně
examples.translation: vlnová funkce je podpořena sadou bázových stavů $\mathcal{S}$, jejichž velikost neroste exponenciálně
examples.why: "support" here is the mathematical support (nosič); "podpořena" reads as "is backed/endorsed by", which flattens the point that the state lives entirely inside a small subspace — the core intuition of the whole SQD section. "bázové sady" is also a calque (elsewhere the file correctly writes "v bázi 6-31G").

examples.source: post-process noisy quantum samples / Post-process results / classical post-processing block
examples.suggested: následně zpracovat zašuměné kvantové vzorky / Zpracování výsledků / Zpracování celé sady vzorků
examples.translation: post-procesovat zašuměné kvantové vzorky / Post-processing výsledků / Post-procesování celé sady vzorků
examples.why: "post-procesovat / post-procesování" is a coined anglicism no Czech technical writer would use; "zpracovat / (následné) zpracování" is the standard rendering, and the file already mixes it with the English noun "post-processing".

examples.source: Self-consistent configuration recovery loop
examples.suggested: Smyčka samokonzistentní obnovy konfigurací
examples.translation: Smyčka sebekonsistentní obnovy konfigurací
examples.why: The established Czech term is "samokonzistentní" (as in samokonzistentní pole/SCF, which this very tutorial computes); "sebekonsistentní" is a calque and additionally uses the non-standard spelling "konsistentní".

examples.source: orbitals for different spins have connections between every 4th orbital (0, 4, 8, etc.)
examples.suggested: jsou orbitaly různých spinů propojeny vždy po každém 4. orbitalu (0, 4, 8 atd.)
examples.translation: mají orbitaly různých spinů propojení každý 4. orbital (0, 4, 8 atd.)
examples.why: The preposition is missing, so the clause is ungrammatical — "propojení každý 4. orbital" has no valid case government. Meaning is recoverable from the figure, but a native editor would rewrite the sentence.

editor_note: The prose itself is fluent, idiomatic Czech with consistent informal register ("naučíš se", "Všimni si", "použij") and good domain phrasing ("koeficienty rozkladu", "matice hustoty", "špatně podmíněné", "soustava lineárních rovnic"), so nothing here misleads a learner — but a native editor would rewrite a lot. The dominant defect is a broken glossary-leak on "circuit": the English word is injected with the Czech ending detached by a space ("Trotterovým Circuit em", "Circuit ů", "Circuit ům", and even "naše obvod y" at the Step-2 bullet), and elsewhere left undeclined where Czech grammar requires a case ("Trotterizované kvantové Circuit", "optimalizují Circuit", "každý z Trotterových Circuit"); the same concept also splits between "Circuit" and "obvod" (line ~282). Three further within-file splits: "observable" is "observabla" at line ~84 but becomes "observace" (= observation, the wrong word) at line ~296; "expectation value" is "střední hodnota" in the Step-4 bullet but "očekávaná hodnota" everywhere after; "Hamiltonian" appears as "Hamiltonián", "Hamiltonianů" and "hamiltonovy dynamiky". Two small fidelity slips: "Heisenberg-like Hamiltonians" loses its "-like" ("Heisenbergových Hamiltonianů", asserting they *are* Heisenberg), and "which can lead to bad performance of the MPF" hardens to a flat consequence ("a tím ke špatnému výkonu MPF").

examples.source: the deepest Trotter circuit that we will actually execute / Trotterized time-evolution circuits
examples.suggested: nejhlubším Trotterovým obvodem ... Trotterizovaných obvodů časové evoluce
examples.translation: nejhlubším Trotterovým Circuit em ... Trotterizovaných Circuit ů časové evoluce
examples.why: Glossary-leak artifact: the English noun is left in place and the Czech declension ending is stranded after a space ('Circuit em', 'Circuit ů', 'Circuit ům'), or dropped entirely so the noun stays undeclined ('Trotterizované kvantové Circuit', 'optimalizují Circuit'). The same run also produced 'naše obvod y' in the Step-2 bullet, so the term is simultaneously split between 'Circuit' and 'obvod'. Ungrammatical Czech and visibly machine-mangled, though the concept stays identifiable.

examples.source: our target observable's expectation values
examples.suggested: střední hodnoty naší cílové observably
examples.translation: očekávané hodnoty naší cílové observace
examples.why: 'observace' means *observation*, not *observable*; the file itself uses the correct 'Observabla' at line ~84 ('Observabla, kterou budeme měřit, je celková magnetizace'). Recognizable in context, but it is the wrong noun for the measured operator.

examples.source: Compute the MPF expectation value / the total expectation values of the MPF
examples.suggested: use 'střední hodnota' throughout (the standard Czech physics term for expectation value)
examples.translation: Výpočet střední hodnoty MPF ... celkové očekávané hodnoty MPF
examples.why: Same concept rendered two ways inside one short file; 'střední hodnota' is the conventional Czech quantum-physics term and appears only in the opening outline, while the whole Step 3/4 discussion switches to 'očekávaná hodnota'.

examples.source: functions to generate Heisenberg-like Hamiltonians on a given connectivity graph
examples.suggested: funkce pro generování hamiltoniánů heisenbergovského typu na daném grafu propojení
examples.translation: funkce pro generování Heisenbergových Hamiltonianů na daném grafu propojení
examples.why: The hedge '-like' is dropped, so the Czech asserts these are Heisenberg Hamiltonians rather than Heisenberg-*like* ones — a dropped qualifier that matters here, since the example actually builds an Ising Hamiltonian with this function.

examples.source: this exact solution can be "ill-conditioned" resulting in very large L1-norms of our coefficients, x, which can lead to bad performance of the MPF
examples.suggested: ..., což vede k velmi velkým L1-normám našich koeficientů $x$, což může vést ke špatnému výkonu MPF
examples.translation: Toto přesné řešení však může být „špatně podmíněné", což vede k velmi velkým L1-normám našich koeficientů $x$, a tím ke špatnému výkonu MPF
examples.why: The second modal ('can lead to') is dropped, turning a possible consequence into a stated one: the Czech reads as if a large L1-norm always ruins MPF performance. Mild strengthening rather than a real inversion, but a native editor would restore 'může vést'.

examples.source: Hamiltonian dynamics / our problem's Hamiltonian / Heisenberg-like Hamiltonians
examples.suggested: pick one stem — 'hamiltonián' declined consistently ('dynamiky hamiltoniánu', 'hamiltoniánů')
examples.translation: hamiltonovy dynamiky (title) / Hamiltoniánu našeho problému / Heisenbergových Hamiltonianů
examples.why: Three renderings of one term in the same file: the adjectival 'hamiltonovy' in the title and section 1b, 'Hamiltoniánu' in the outline/heading, and the half-anglicized 'Hamiltonianů' (missing the long á) in the body.

examples.source: a simple line of 10 qubits / an approximate model
examples.suggested: jednoduchou řadu 10 qubitů ... use either 'přibližný' or 'aproximativní' consistently
examples.translation: jednoduchou řadu 10 Qubitů ... aproximativního modelu ... přibližný model
examples.why: 'Qubitů' is capitalized mid-sentence (another leak artifact — the term is lowercase everywhere in normal Czech text), and the approximate model is 'aproximativní' in both its headings but 'přibližný' in the concluding paragraph. Cosmetic, but exactly what a native technical editor would clean up.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inversions, no dropped caveats, "du" register holds consistently ("findest du", "ersetze einfach", "Beachte") and the domain core is solid (Krylow-Basiszustände, Trotterisierung, Ein-Störstellen-Anderson-Modell, Teilraumdimensionen, transpilieren). What a native technical editor would change is surface: "fake backend" is rendered "gefälschtes 127-Qubit-Backend" ("counterfeit/forged" — German docs say Fake-Backend or simuliertes/nachgebildetes Backend), and "across all batches' solutions" is calqued as "über alle Batches' Lösungen", an English Saxon genitive that is simply ungrammatical in German. "circuit" is split within the file between "Circuits" (lines 20, 33, 64, 140, 148, 159, 161) and "Quantenschaltkreis(e)/Zeitentwicklungsschaltkreise" (lines 18, 30, 64) — recognizable either way, but inconsistent. Smaller items: "Das Muster lässt sich in vier Schritte beschreiben" (wrong case/collocation; "in vier Schritten beschreiben" or "in vier Schritte gliedern"), the untouched English possessive "Qiskit's PauliEvolutionGate", "Qiskit IBM Runtime-Dokumenten" (should be -Dokumentation), and the binomial idiom rendered "(Anzahl_Orbitale wähle nelec_a)" where German uses "über", while the very next expression keeps English `(8 choose 4)**2`.

examples.source: We will use a fake 127-qubit backend from ``qiskit_ibm_runtime`` to emulate a real device. To run on a real QPU, just replace the fake backend with a real backend.
examples.suggested: Wir verwenden ein Fake-Backend mit 127 Qubits aus ``qiskit_ibm_runtime``, um ein echtes Gerät zu emulieren. Um auf einer echten QPU zu rechnen, ersetze das Fake-Backend einfach durch ein echtes Backend.
examples.translation: Wir verwenden ein gefälschtes 127-Qubit-Backend aus ``qiskit_ibm_runtime``, um ein echtes Gerät zu emulieren. Um auf einem echten QPU zu laufen, ersetze einfach das gefälschte Backend durch ein echtes Backend.
examples.why: "gefälscht" means counterfeit/forged and carries a deception connotation; a Qiskit FakeBackend is a calibrated stand-in, and German Qiskit material keeps "Fake-Backend" (or says "simuliert"). Also "einem echten QPU" — QPU takes feminine agreement ("einer echten QPU").

examples.source: The second plot shows the average occupancy of each spatial orbital across all batches' solutions.
examples.suggested: Der zweite Plot zeigt die mittlere Besetzung jedes räumlichen Orbitals über die Lösungen aller Batches hinweg.
examples.translation: Der zweite Plot zeigt die mittlere Besetzung jedes räumlichen Orbitals über alle Batches' Lösungen.
examples.why: The English Saxon genitive is copied verbatim; "Batches' Lösungen" is not a possible German construction and reads as raw MT in an otherwise clean paragraph.

examples.source: Transpile the circuits for the backend / Trotterized time-evolution circuits / a set of Trotterized quantum circuits
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering for "circuit" and hold it (either "Schaltkreis(e)" throughout, or "Circuit(s)" throughout, including the Step-1 heading).
examples.translation: Die Circuits für das Backend transpilieren / trotterisierte Zeitentwicklungsschaltkreise / eine Menge trotterisierter Quantenschaltkreise
examples.why: Within one file the same object alternates between the English "Circuits" and "(Quanten-)Schaltkreise", sometimes in adjacent sentences (line 64 has both); the concept stays identifiable, but the split is exactly the inconsistency a technical editor would unify.

examples.source: The pattern can be described in four steps:
examples.suggested: Das Muster lässt sich in vier Schritten beschreiben:  (oder: … in vier Schritte gliedern:)
examples.translation: Das Muster lässt sich in vier Schritte beschreiben:
examples.why: "in" + accusative with "beschreiben" is a case error produced by tracking the English preposition; German needs dative ("in vier Schritten beschreiben") or a different verb ("in vier Schritte gliedern/unterteilen").

examples.source: the full Hilbert space is dimension ``(num_orbitals choose nelec_a) * (num_orbitals choose nelec_b)``. So for this problem: `(8 choose 4)**2 = 4900`.
examples.suggested: … die Dimension ``(Anzahl_Orbitale über nelec_a) * (Anzahl_Orbitale über nelec_b)`` … (or leave both expressions in English, as the second one is)
examples.translation: Der vollständige Hilbert-Raum hat die Dimension ``(Anzahl_Orbitale wähle nelec_a) * (Anzahl_Orbitale wähle nelec_b)``. Für dieses Problem gilt daher: `(8 choose 4)**2 = 4900`.
examples.why: The binomial coefficient "n choose k" is "n über k" in German; "wähle" reads as the imperative "choose!" and does not name the operation. It also clashes with the very next expression, which keeps the English "choose" untranslated.

examples.source: Check out the [Qiskit IBM Runtime docs] for more info.
examples.suggested: Weitere Informationen findest du in der [Qiskit IBM Runtime-Dokumentation].
examples.translation: Weitere Informationen findest du in den [Qiskit IBM Runtime-Dokumenten].
examples.why: "Dokumente" means individual documents/files; the reference is to the documentation as a whole ("Dokumentation"), which is also what the file uses correctly at line 181 ("API-Dokumentation").

editor_note: Solid, faithful translation with correct core terminology (Basissatz, Rechenbasis, Erzeugungs-/Vernichtungsoperatoren, Grundzustandsenergie, Teilraum, dünnbesetzt) and a consistent informal "du" register ("ersetze einfach", "findest du", "Bedenke"). Four editorial defects, none misleading: (1) "one- and two-body electronic integrals" is rendered "ein- und zweiteilige elektronische Integrale" — "zweiteilig" means "consisting of two parts", not "two-body"; the field says "Ein- und Zweiteilchen-Integrale" (or "Zwei-Elektronen-Integrale"). (2) The mathematical "set" is rendered two ways in the same paragraph — correctly as "Menge von Basiszuständen" (line 49) but as "Satz" for $\tilde{\mathcal{X}}$ and for "the full set of bitstring samples" (lines 25, 53); "Satz" in German mathematics reads as "theorem". (3) The restrictive "only" in "produce samples of the members of $\mathcal{S}$ only" is dropped (line 53), losing the emphasis that this is the device's entire job. (4) "the wave function is supported in a set of basis states" is calqued as "ist auf einer Menge ... getragen", which no German physicist would write ("hat ihren Träger in ...").

examples.source: $h_{pr}$ and $(pr|qs)$ are the one- and two-body electronic integrals.
examples.suggested: $h_{pr}$ und $(pr|qs)$ sind die Ein- und Zweiteilchen-Integrale (Ein- bzw. Zwei-Elektronen-Integrale).
examples.translation: $h_{pr}$ und $(pr|qs)$ sind die ein- und zweiteiligen elektronischen Integrale.
examples.why: "two-body" is a many-body-physics term (Zweiteilchen-/Zwei-Elektronen-), not "zweiteilig" = "consisting of two parts". The adjacent formula makes the intent recoverable, so it is an imperfect-but-decodable term rather than a false concept.

examples.source: yielding the set of noisy configurations $\tilde{\mathcal{X}}$ ... The set $\tilde{\mathcal{X}}$ is then passed into the classical post-processing block
examples.suggested: was die Menge verrauschter Konfigurationen $\tilde{\mathcal{X}}$ ergibt ... Die Menge $\tilde{\mathcal{X}}$ wird dann an den klassischen Nachbearbeitungsblock übergeben
examples.translation: was den Satz verrauschter Konfigurationen $\tilde{\mathcal{X}}$ ergibt ... Der Satz $\tilde{\mathcal{X}}$ wird dann an den klassischen Nachbearbeitungsblock übergeben
examples.why: The same file already uses the correct "Menge von Basiszuständen" four lines earlier (line 49), so "set" is split between "Menge" and "Satz" within one paragraph; "Satz" additionally collides with the German word for "theorem".

examples.source: The role of the quantum device is to produce samples of the members of $\mathcal{S}$ only.
examples.suggested: Die Rolle des Quantengeräts besteht ausschließlich darin, Samples der Elemente von $\mathcal{S}$ zu erzeugen.
examples.translation: Die Rolle des Quantengeräts besteht darin, Samples der Elemente von $\mathcal{S}$ zu erzeugen.
examples.why: The restrictive "only" is dropped. The sentence remains true, but the pedagogical point — that this is the quantum device's entire contribution — is flattened.

examples.source: the wave function is supported in a set of basis states $\mathcal{S} = \{|x\rangle \}$ whose size does not increase exponentially
examples.suggested: Die Wellenfunktion hat ihren Träger in einer Menge von Basiszuständen $\mathcal{S} = \{|x\rangle \}$, deren Größe nicht exponentiell ... wächst
examples.translation: Die Wellenfunktion ist auf einer Menge von Basiszuständen $\mathcal{S} = \{|x\rangle \}$ getragen, deren Größe nicht exponentiell ... wächst
examples.why: "ist auf ... getragen" is a word-for-word calque of English "is supported on"; German uses the noun ("hat ihren Träger in") or "wird von ... aufgespannt". Grammatical but unmistakably translated.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I found no semantic drift, no inverted conditions, no dropped caveats, and the informal "tú" register holds ("verifica", "echa un vistazo", "No dudes en postularte"; "Consulta"/"utiliza" are tú-forms, not usted). The defects are terminological and grammatical. (1) Glossary leaks: the English word "Circuit(s)" survives capitalized mid-sentence six times ("crear tu primer Circuit cuántico", "tus Circuits en el computador cuántico real", "a nivel de Circuits cuánticos extendidos", "optimización de Circuits cuánticos", "diseñar manualmente tus Circuits cuánticos", the heading "Prácticas: Circuits cuánticos usando puertas de un solo qubit") while the rest of the file correctly says "circuito(s) cuántico(s)"; "Gates" leaks twice ("una secuencia de Gates $Z$ y $X$", "aplicar los diferentes Gates"). (2) "gate" is split three ways within one file: "puerta" dominates §3 (25 hits) and "compuerta" dominates §4–§5 (15 hits: "compuerta canónica de dos qubits", "compuerta Hadamard", "conjuntos de compuertas nativas"), plus the English "Gates" — both Spanish terms are defensible, but the file should pick one. (3) Gender agreement is broken five times by what looks like a blind gate→puerta substitution: "el puerta de Hadamard", "el puerta $Z$", "el puerta $S^\dagger$", "un puerta $Y$", "elige un puerta"; also "que es el primero (y en este caso único) qubit" (should be "el primer"). (4) "Circuit Composer" (the product) becomes "el circuito Composer" twice and "nuestro widget de Circuit". (5) "statevector" is left in English once ("El statevector que se usa aquí") though §5 correctly says "vector de estado". (6) Minor translationese: "We're breezing through this overview" → "Nos estamos acelerando en este resumen" (a native would write "Vamos a pasar rápido por este resumen"), and English title-casing calqued into the section labels ("Los Estados de Un Solo qubit", "Cuestionario Cuántico con Compuertas Multi-Qubit", "Información Adicional").

examples.source: make your first quantum circuit ... Run you circuits on the real quantum computer
examples.suggested: crear tu primer circuito cuántico, ... ejecutar tus circuitos en el computador cuántico real
examples.translation: crear tu primer Circuit cuántico, ... ejecutar tus Circuits en el computador cuántico real
examples.why: Untranslated, capitalized English 'Circuit(s)' leaks into Spanish prose in six places while the same file elsewhere uses the correct 'circuito(s) cuántico(s)' — a within-file split of the most basic term in the lesson.

examples.source: quantum gates / the canonical two qubit gate / Hadamard gate
examples.suggested: pick one convention for the whole file (e.g. 'compuerta' throughout, or 'puerta' throughout)
