examples.why: "overhead" is consistently rendered "costo", but the same file uses "costo" for genuine cost ("eficiencia de costos", "**Rentabilidad**" for Cost-effectiveness), blurring two distinct concepts the English keeps apart. "Sobrecarga" is the conventional Spanish term in error-mitigation literature.

examples.source: They are in preview release status and subject to change.
examples.suggested: Se encuentran en estado de vista previa y están sujetas a cambios.
examples.translation: Se encuentran en estado de vista previa sujeta a cambios.
examples.why: Gender agreement attaches "sujeta" to "vista previa", so the sentence says the preview status is subject to change rather than the Qiskit Functions themselves; it also collapses two coordinated predicates into one modifier.

examples.source: A Qiskit Function by Algorithmiq
examples.suggested: Una Función (Qiskit Function) de Algorithmiq
examples.translation: Una Función (Qiskit Function) por Algorithmiq
examples.why: "por Algorithmiq" is a direct calque of English "by"; Spanish uses "de" (or "desarrollada por", which the description on line 4 already uses) — the same attribution is rendered two ways inside one file.

examples.source: TEM has the potential to enable quantum advantage in complex scenarios
examples.suggested: TEM tiene el potencial de hacer posible la ventaja cuántica en escenarios complejos
examples.translation: TEM tiene el potencial de habilitar la ventaja cuántica en escenarios complejos
examples.why: "habilitar" is a calque of "enable" used in the software sense (enable a feature); for a capability becoming attainable a native technical writer writes "posibilitar" or "hacer posible".

examples.source: an informationally complete positive operator-valued measure (IC-POVM)
examples.suggested: una medida de valores de operador positivos informacionalmente completa (IC-POVM)
examples.translation: una medida de operador con valor positivo informacionalmente completa (IC-POVM)
examples.why: Word-by-word rendering of the English compound misplaces the modifiers (it reads as "a measure of an operator with a positive value"); the standard Spanish expansion of POVM is "medida de valores de operador positivos". Recognizable, not misleading, but a native editor would fix it.

editor_note: Nothing in this file would mislead a learner: the physics prose is accurate (pureza reducida, entrelazamiento, fase cuántica, q-esfera, base computacional are all correct and consistent, and "puerta/qubit/disparos/backend" hold throughout). What a native technical editor would still change is a layer of calqued syntax and two small fidelity slips: "la puerta CNOT ... cuesta mucho más tiempo para ejecutar en hardware real" (word-for-word "costs much more time to execute"; Spanish wants "tarda mucho más en ejecutarse"), "cuando exploras ... en pequeños números de qubits", "en algunos hardwares", and the endlessly repeated table note "el número de qubits necesarios para admitir la puerta", where "admitir" is a poor rendering of "to support" (should be "que requiere la puerta"). Fidelity slips: the Visualizations bullet drops the contrastive "instead" ("para obtener resultados del backend especificado" loses that this replaces the simulated visualizations), and the IBM plan names Open/Flex are over-translated to "Planes Abierto, Flexible o Premium", which no longer match the UI the learner sees. One grammar slip: "(u unos)" must be "(o unos)" — "u" is only used before o-/ho-.

examples.source: Because the two-qubit CNOT gate costs much more time to execute on real hardware than single qubit gates, circuit cost is sometimes measured in the number of CNOT gates.
examples.suggested: Dado que la puerta CNOT de dos qubits tarda mucho más en ejecutarse en hardware real que las puertas de un solo qubit, el coste de un circuito a veces se mide por el número de puertas CNOT.
examples.translation: Debido a que la puerta CNOT de dos qubits cuesta mucho más tiempo para ejecutar en hardware real que las puertas de un solo qubit, el costo del circuito a veces se mide en el número de puertas CNOT.
examples.why: 'cuesta ... tiempo para ejecutar' is a word-for-word calque of 'costs time to execute'; no Spanish technical writer would phrase gate duration this way.

examples.source: Sign in and click **Run circuit** to get results from the specified backend instead.
examples.suggested: Inicia sesión y haz clic en **Ejecutar circuito** para obtener, en su lugar, resultados del backend especificado.
examples.translation: Inicia sesión y haz clic en **Ejecutar circuito** para obtener resultados del backend especificado.
examples.why: The contrastive 'instead' is dropped, so the sentence no longer says these results REPLACE the single-shot simulated visualizations described just before.

examples.source: an instance, which is associated with a plan (such as the Open, Flex, or Premium Plans)
examples.suggested: una instancia, que está asociada con un plan (como los planes Open, Flex o Premium)
examples.translation: una instancia, que está asociada con un plan (como los Planes Abierto, Flexible o Premium)
examples.why: Open/Flex are IBM Quantum product names shown untranslated in the UI; rendering them as 'Abierto'/'Flexible' makes them unfindable for the reader.

examples.source: where n is the number of qubits needed to support the gate
examples.suggested: donde n es el número de qubits que requiere la puerta
examples.translation: donde n es el número de qubits necesarios para admitir la puerta
examples.why: 'admitir' means 'to accept/allow in', not 'to support' in the sense of 'be sufficient for'; the calque is repeated in ~20 identical table cells, so it dominates the page.

examples.source: Basis states with the same number of zeros (or ones) lie on a shared latitude
examples.suggested: Los estados de base con el mismo número de ceros (o unos) se encuentran en una misma latitud
examples.translation: Los estados de base con el mismo número de ceros (u unos) se encuentran en una latitud compartida
examples.why: 'u' replaces 'o' only before words beginning with o-/ho-; before 'unos' it is ungrammatical.

examples.source: when exploring quantum applications and algorithms on small numbers of qubits
examples.suggested: cuando exploras aplicaciones y algoritmos cuánticos con pocos qubits
examples.translation: cuando exploras aplicaciones cuánticas y algoritmos en pequeños números de qubits
examples.why: 'en pequeños números de qubits' is a literal transfer of the English prepositional phrase; Spanish says 'con pocos qubits' / 'con un número reducido de qubits'.

examples.source: The Toffoli gate, also known as the double controlled-NOT gate (CCX)
examples.suggested: La puerta Toffoli, también conocida como puerta NOT doblemente controlada (CCX)
examples.translation: La puerta Toffoli, también conocida como puerta NOT controlado doble (CCX)
examples.why: 'NOT controlado doble' leaves the modifier ungoverned and mismatched in gender; the concept is still recognizable but the phrasing is not idiomatic.

examples.source: On some hardwares, it is a native gate that can be implemented with a π/2 or X90 pulse.
examples.suggested: En algunos equipos, es una puerta nativa que se puede implementar con un pulso π/2 o X90.
examples.translation: En algunos hardwares, es una puerta nativa que se puede implementar con un pulso π/2 o X90.
examples.why: 'hardwares' is not a valid Spanish plural (hardware is uncountable); the English source's own oddity was carried over verbatim.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no inverted conditions, no dropped caveats, and the "tu" register holds from the intro to "bon calcul quantique !". The dominant defect is that "gate" is rendered four ways inside one file: untranslated "gates" (§1–2: "temps d'opération des gates", "erreurs de gates", "gates CNOT", "tu appliques des gates au début"), correct "portes" (§3–5: "portes quantiques", "portes de base"), capitalized "Gates"/"Gate" ("Gates de base", "de nombreux Gates séquentiels", "un Gate complexe à 3 qubits", "Tout autre Gate"), and "Gates universels" in the conclusion — with the same split hitting "Backend"/"backend", "Transpiler", and "multi-Qubit". Worse, wherever "porte" is used it repeatedly takes masculine agreement, which is ungrammatical in French (porte is feminine): "un porte de Toffoli", "un porte non natif", "les portes natifs", "les portes universels", "le porte quantique correct", "Gates de base natifs". Neither problem misleads — a learner still identifies the concept — but a native technical editor would normalize every occurrence to "porte(s) … quantique(s)" with feminine agreement, and lowercase "backend"/"transpileur". Smaller nits: "comptes" vs "comptages" for counts within §5, and "feed-forward control" flattened to "contrôle en aval".

examples.source: We'll take a non-native gate (like a 3-qubit Toffoli gate, CCX) and see how it breaks down into the device's basis gates.
examples.suggested: On va prendre une porte non native (comme une porte de Toffoli à 3 qubits, CCX) et voir comment elle se décompose en portes de base du dispositif.
examples.translation: On va prendre un porte non natif (comme un porte de Toffoli à 3 qubits, CCX) et voir comment il se décompose en Gates de base du dispositif.
examples.why: Three defects in one sentence: masculine agreement on the feminine noun "porte" (twice, plus the pronoun "il"), and the English "Gates" capitalized mid-sentence where the surrounding paragraph already uses "portes".

examples.source: gate operation time / A universal set of quantum gates
examples.suggested: Use "portes" everywhere: "le temps d'opération des portes", "un ensemble universel de portes quantiques".
examples.translation: le temps d'opération des gates … Un ensemble universel de gates quantiques (§Introduction) — vs — le temps d'opération des portes … Un ensemble universel de portes quantiques (§3, §4)
examples.why: The intro and §1–2 keep the English "gates" while §3–5 correctly translate it as "portes"; the very same criterion statement appears in both renderings, so the reader meets two words for one concept within a single document.

examples.source: This proves that the native gates are sufficient to express the Toffoli. / The ibmq_brisbane device uses the Eagle architecture with basis gates shown above.
examples.suggested: Cela prouve que les portes natives sont suffisantes pour exprimer la porte de Toffoli. / … avec les portes de base indiquées ci-dessus.
examples.translation: Cela prouve que les portes natifs sont suffisants pour exprimer le Toffoli. / … avec les portes de base indiqués ci-dessus.
examples.why: Recurring masculine agreement on "porte" reads as unrevised machine output to a French technical reader; a native writer would never write "les portes natifs … suffisants".

examples.source: apply the correct quantum gate on Bob's qubit to perfectly recover the original state
examples.suggested: appliquer la porte quantique adéquate sur le qubit de Bob pour récupérer parfaitement l'état original
examples.translation: appliquer le porte quantique correct sur le qubit de Bob pour récupérer parfaitement l'état original
examples.why: "le porte" is not a valid French noun phrase here; the same gender slip surfaces in the teaching-heavy teleportation paragraph, where prose polish matters most.

examples.source: We'll use a fake backend with known T1/T2 times. / the basis gates for a typical IBM backend / These are the primitive operations the hardware natively supports
examples.suggested: un faux backend … / les portes de base d'un backend IBM typique / … (porte sqrt(X), porte X …)
examples.translation: On utilisera un faux Backend avec des temps T1/T2 connus. / les portes de base d'un Backend IBM typique / Ce sont les opérations primitives que le matériel supporte nativement (… Gate sqrt(X), Gate X …)
examples.why: Mid-sentence capitalization of "Backend", "Gate", "Transpiler" and "multi-Qubit" is a German-style noun-capitalization calque that no French technical writer uses; French keeps these lowercase.

editor_note: Faithful, idiomatic and consistently informal ("Suis ces étapes", "Ignore cette étape si tu utilises…"); IBM/IAM terminology is correct and stable throughout (access groups → "groupes d'accès", resource groups → "groupes de ressources", service instances → "instances du service IBM Quantum", ID provider → "fournisseur d'identité", allowlist → "liste d'autorisation", preview service → "service … en préversion"), and the tricky step-1 logic ("The `enabled` setting restricts user visibility" → "Le paramètre `enabled` restreint la visibilité des utilisateurs", plus the `disabled` recommendation for API key creation) is preserved without inversion.

Nothing here misleads — every prose paragraph is semantically faithful (the "Open Plan users cannot submit session jobs" caveat, the pre/post-processing overhead sentence, and the PUB definition all survive intact), and the keep-English convention (Circuit, Gates, Backend-ים, observables, PUB) is applied consistently throughout. Three things a native technical editor would still change: (1) "expectation value" is rendered "ערך הציפייה" (§1), a literal calque of "expectation" — the conventional Hebrew physics/statistics term is "ערך התוחלת"/"התוחלת"; recognizable, but not the field's word. (2) "transpile" is used as a bare English noun where a verb is needed — "עבר Transpiler למחרוזת חדשה" (§2 intro) and "למד איך לבצע Transpiler מקומי" (Next steps) both read as "underwent/perform a Transpiler"; a native writer would write "עבר טרנספילציה" / "לבצע טרנספילציה מקומית" (or "לבצע Transpile"). (3) Minor stiffness in §5: "תקורת עיבוד מוקדמת קוונטית ... ותקורת עיבוד מאוחרת קלאסית" stacks three post-modifiers awkwardly and uses "עיבוד מוקדם" where Hebrew technical usage is "עיבוד מקדים".

examples.source: You can then select the device you want to use to calculate the expectation value.
examples.suggested: ... כדי לחשב את ערך התוחלת.
examples.translation: אחר כך אפשר לבחור את המכשיר שבו תרצה להשתמש כדי לחשב את ערך הציפייה.
examples.why: "ערך הציפייה" is a word-for-word calque of "expectation"; the established Hebrew term for the quantum/statistical expectation value is "תוחלת" (ערך התוחלת). Recognizable, so not misleading, but it is not the term a Hebrew-speaking quantum engineer would write.

examples.source: ...the `qasm_string` has been transpiled to a new string `resulting_qasm`. / Learn how to transpile locally in the Transpile section.
examples.suggested: ...שה-`qasm_string` עבר טרנספילציה למחרוזת חדשה... / למד איך לבצע טרנספילציה מקומית בסעיף Transpile.
examples.translation: ...שה-`qasm_string` עבר Transpiler למחרוזת חדשה `resulting_qasm`. / למד איך לבצע Transpiler מקומי בסעיף Transpile.
examples.why: The English verb "transpile" is substituted by the tool noun "Transpiler", producing "underwent a Transpiler" / "perform a local Transpiler" — ungrammatical as a Hebrew verb phrase and a clear MT fingerprint. The process noun (טרנספילציה) or the verb form is what a native writer uses.

examples.source: This typically results in quantum pre-processing overhead related to model training, and classical post-processing overhead to mitigate errors in the raw results...
examples.suggested: בדרך כלל נוצרת תקורה של עיבוד מקדים קוונטי הקשור לאימון המודל, ותקורה של עיבוד מאוחר קלאסי לצמצום השגיאות בתוצאות הגולמיות...
examples.translation: בדרך כלל הדבר גורם לתקורת עיבוד מוקדמת קוונטית הקשורה לאימון המודל, ולתקורת עיבוד מאוחרת קלאסית לצמצום שגיאות בתוצאות הגולמיות...
examples.why: Three stacked post-modifiers ("תקורת עיבוד מוקדמת קוונטית") force the reader to re-parse which adjective attaches to what; "עיבוד מקדים" is also the standard Hebrew rendering of pre-processing, not "עיבוד מוקדם". Meaning is intact — it just reads as translated rather than written.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, dropped caveats or swapped quantities; the H2/LiH/ethene worked examples, the 276-term count, the total-minus-nuclear-repulsion energy explanation and the ZZII ordering example all match the English. What a native technical editor would change: (1) "annihilation operator" is rendered "אופרטור אפסה" (lines 44, 181, 217) — "אפסה" is not the Hebrew physics term; the field says "אופרטורי יצירה והשמדה". (2) Line 48 has a genuine wrong word: "הם מציתים סטטיסטיקה שונה לחלוטין" — "מציתים" means "they ignite"; it should be "מצייתים לסטטיסטיקה שונה לחלוטין" ("obey"). (3) "mapper" is rendered "מפה" (frontmatter, lines 324, 516, 521), i.e. a cartographic map, while "mapping" is correctly "מיפוי" elsewhere (45, 183, 185, 217) — an internal split; "ממפֶּה"/"כלי מיפוי" is wanted. (4) Scattered calques and typos: "אנחנו מגיבים להלן" for "we comment below" (185), "לדגמון" for "לדגמן" (100), "נתן" for "ניתן" (93), "ה-Gate-ים" where Hebrew has the settled "השערים" (519), and the reversed voice in "Qubitים 0 ו-1 פועלים על ידי אופרטור הזהות" (519), which should be "שעליהם פועל אופרטור הזהות". None of these teach a false concept, but they read as fluent MT rather than native technical Hebrew.

examples.source: Generate the fermionic Hamiltonian (creation and annihilation operators)
examples.suggested: צור את ההמילטוניאן הפרמיוני (אופרטורי יצירה והשמדה)
examples.translation: צור את ההמילטוניאן הפרמיוני (אופרטורי יצירה ואפסה)
examples.why: "אפסה" is a coinage from "אפס" (zero) and is not the conventional Hebrew term for an annihilation operator; Hebrew physics writing uses "אופרטור השמדה" (or "איון"). Recognizable from context and used consistently, so MINOR — but no native chemist would write it.

examples.source: That means they obey completely different statistics from distinguishable, bosonic qubits.
examples.suggested: פירוש הדבר שהם מצייתים לסטטיסטיקה שונה לחלוטין מזו של קיוביטים בוזוניים הניתנים להבחנה.
examples.translation: פירוש הדבר שהם מציתים סטטיסטיקה שונה לחלוטין מ-Qubitים בוזוניים הניתנים להבחנה.
examples.why: "מציתים" means "they set fire to" — the intended verb is "מצייתים ל..." (obey), and the preposition ל is missing too, so the clause is literally "they ignite statistics". The physics still lands, but the sentence is garbled Hebrew.

examples.source: using a custom Jordan-Wigner mapper / some offering multiple mappers / using any available mapper
examples.suggested: ממפֶּה Jordan-Wigner מותאם אישית / מציעות כלי מיפוי מרובים / תוך שימוש בכל ממפֶּה זמין
examples.translation: שימוש במפה Jordan-Wigner מותאמת אישית / מציעות מפות מרובות / תוך שימוש בכל מפה זמינה
examples.why: "מפה" is a cartographic map (or a tablecloth), not a mapper. The file correctly uses "מיפוי" for "mapping" in lines 45/183/185/217, so the agent noun is both wrong and inconsistent with the file's own convention.

examples.source: We comment below on syntax considerations for other solutions.
examples.suggested: נעיר להלן על שיקולי תחביר בפתרונות אחרים.
examples.translation: אנחנו מגיבים להלן על שיקולי תחביר לפתרונות אחרים.
examples.why: "מגיבים" is "we react/respond" — a literal calque of English "comment". A Hebrew technical writer would use "נעיר" or "נתייחס", and would use the future tense that Hebrew prose uses for forward references.

examples.source: ...would write the term [Z2 Z3] as ZZII (qubits 0 and 1 being acting on by the identity operator, qubits 2 and 3 being acted on by the Z operator...)
examples.suggested: ...(אופרטור הזהות פועל על קיוביטים 0 ו-1, ואופרטור Z פועל על קיוביטים 2 ו-3, בסדר שבו קיוביט 0 הוא הימני ביותר).
examples.translation: ...שיכתבו את המונח `[Z2 Z3]` כ-`ZZII` (Qubitים 0 ו-1 פועלים על ידי אופרטור הזהות, Qubitים 2 ו-3 פועלים על ידי אופרטור Z, מסודרים כאשר Qubit 0 נמצא הרחק ביותר מימין).
examples.why: "Qubitים 0 ו-1 פועלים על ידי..." reverses the agent — it reads as the qubits acting by means of the operator. Also "נמצא הרחק ביותר מימין" parses as "farthest from the right", the opposite of "rightmost"; the ZZII example rescues the meaning, but the ordering convention should be stated as "הימני ביותר". Same line renders "gates" as "ה-Gate-ים" where Hebrew has the settled "השערים".

editor_note: Nothing here misleads: all technical content (2 cuts, sampling overhead 127.06, "maksimum 4 qubit per subcircuit", "satu wire cut dan memotong satu CRZGate", "Langkah 3 dan 4 dari pola Qiskit ... seperti pada tutorial sebelumnya") is faithful, and cut/observable/subcircuit terminology is consistent. Two editorial problems remain. First, the Qiskit-pattern step names are rendered inconsistently: "Step 1: Map" becomes the bare noun "Langkah 1: Peta" (a cartographic map) while "Step 2: Optimize" correctly becomes the verb "Langkah 2: Optimalkan"; the step is the mapping action, so "Petakan"/"Pemetaan" is what a native technical writer would use, and the noun/verb split makes the two step titles look like different kinds of thing. Second, kept-English glossary terms are capitalized mid-sentence throughout ("Buat Circuit dan observable", "pemotongan Gate dan wire ini", "dijalankan di Backend", alt text "Diagram Circuit kuantum"), which reads as a glossary-substitution artifact rather than Indonesian prose — lowercase, or the standard "sirkuit"/"gerbang", would be the native rendering, and note that the very same file already lowercases "wire cut", "subcircuit" and "observable", so the capitalization is not even internally consistent.

examples.source: ## Step 1: Map
examples.suggested: ## Langkah 1: Petakan
examples.translation: ## Langkah 1: Peta
examples.why: "Peta" is the noun for a geographic map; the Qiskit-pattern step is the act of mapping the problem onto circuits. It also clashes with the sibling heading "Langkah 2: Optimalkan", which is correctly an imperative verb.

examples.source: Create a circuit and observables / cutting these gates and wires / run on the backend
examples.suggested: Buat sirkuit dan observable / pemotongan gate dan wire ini / dijalankan di backend
examples.translation: Buat Circuit dan observable / pemotongan Gate dan wire ini / dijalankan di Backend
examples.why: Mid-sentence capitals on Circuit/Gate/Backend are a glossary-substitution artifact; Indonesian does not capitalize common nouns, and the same file already writes "wire", "subcircuit" and "observable" in lowercase.

examples.source: Quantum circuit diagram
examples.suggested: Diagram sirkuit kuantum
examples.translation: Diagram Circuit kuantum
examples.why: The alt text mixes an English head noun with an Indonesian adjective and a stray capital; a native writer would use either fully Indonesian "sirkuit kuantum" or fully English "quantum circuit", not the hybrid.

editor_note: No semantic drift: every claim, quantity and caveat matches the English (the "sisa error Trotter lebih kecil daripada ... nilai $k_j$ terbesar" point, the L1-norm caveat, and the closing admission that the approximate model is "lebih buruk dari solusi eksak" are all faithful), and the informal "kamu" register holds throughout. The defects are terminological consistency and translationese. "circuit" is rendered as English capitalized "Circuit" mid-sentence roughly a dozen times ("Circuit Trotter terdalam", "eksekusi Circuit", "Circuit kuantum Trotterized", "mengoptimalkan Circuit") but once as Indonesian "sirkuit" at line 117 — a visible glossary-substitution artifact; likewise "static" is left English in the heading "Pengantar static MPF" while the very next line uses "MPF _statis_". Two calqued passages read as MT rather than native technical Indonesian: "anggaran langkah Trotter yang tetap yang bisa kamu eksekusi" (financial "anggaran" for a step budget, plus a stacked yang…yang) and "Nilai terkecil dimotivasi oleh target waktu evolusi ... yang biasanya memberitahu kita untuk memenuhi".

examples.source: you can use MPF to find several shorter-depth circuits to run
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering for "circuit" and use it everywhere — e.g. "sirkuit" throughout ("sirkuit Trotter terdalam", "eksekusi sirkuit", "sirkuit kuantum Trotterized")
examples.translation: kamu bisa menggunakan MPF untuk menemukan beberapa sirkuit dengan kedalaman lebih pendek
examples.why: The file mixes an English capitalized "Circuit" mid-sentence (~12 occurrences) with a single Indonesian "sirkuit" here. The concept stays identifiable, but the capitalized English noun inside Indonesian prose reads as an automated glossary substitution, not as something a native technical writer produced.

examples.source: An introduction to static MPFs / _Static_ MPFs are those where...
examples.suggested: Pengantar MPF statis
examples.translation: Pengantar static MPF / MPF _statis_ adalah yang nilai $x_j$-nya **TIDAK** bergantung...
examples.why: The heading keeps English "static" while the sentence immediately below it translates the same modifier as "statis"; the section title and its body should not disagree on the term the section is named after.

examples.source: For a fixed budget of Trotter steps that you are able to execute, you can obtain results with a Trotter error that is smaller in total.
examples.suggested: Dengan jatah langkah Trotter tetap yang mampu kamu eksekusi, kamu bisa memperoleh hasil dengan total error Trotter yang lebih kecil.
examples.translation: Untuk anggaran langkah Trotter yang tetap yang bisa kamu eksekusi, kamu bisa mendapatkan hasil dengan error Trotter yang lebih kecil secara total.
examples.why: "anggaran" is the financial sense of budget and is a calque here; "jatah"/"kuota" is what an Indonesian technical writer would use for an execution budget. The stacked "yang tetap yang bisa" is also a syntactic carry-over from the English relative clause chain.

examples.source: The smallest value is motivated by the target evolution time of $t=8.0$ which normally tells us to satisfy $t/k_{\text{min}} \lt 1$
examples.suggested: Nilai terkecil didasari oleh target waktu evolusi $t=8.0$, yang biasanya mengharuskan kita memenuhi $t/k_{\text{min}} \lt 1$
examples.translation: Nilai terkecil dimotivasi oleh target waktu evolusi $t=8.0$ yang biasanya memberitahu kita untuk memenuhi $t/k_{\text{min}} \lt 1$
examples.why: "dimotivasi oleh" and "memberitahu kita untuk memenuhi" are word-for-word renderings of "is motivated by" / "tells us to satisfy"; a native writer would say "didasari/dilatarbelakangi" and "mengharuskan kita memenuhi". Meaning is intact, but the sentence reads as translated rather than written.

editor_note: No semantic drift found: every claim, quantity and caveat matches the English (six observables, ⟨Z₁Z₀⟩ = 1 vs zero, the "only for a small circuit" caveat in the simulator note, the decay of ⟨Z₀Z_i⟩ with increasing i), core terminology is correct and consistent ("valore di aspettazione", "gli osservabili", qubit/gate/backend/job/entanglement kept in English as the field does), and the informal "tu" holds throughout ("Consulta", "Nota che", "devi anche considerare") with no Lei slips. What a native editor would still change: "utility level"/"utility-scale" is rendered two different ways in the same file — "a livello di utilità" (intro) vs "a scala di utilità" (Scale section) — and neither is the idiomatic "su scala di utilità"; the bit-ordering admonition leaves the English ordinal inside Italian prose, "l'$n^{th}$ cifra", which no Italian technical writer would write ("la cifra $n$-esima"). Two calques remain: "quanta resilienza costruire contro gli errori" (a word-for-word trace of "how much resilience to build against errors") and "trasforma il circuito e gli osservabili per corrispondere all'ISA" ("to match" → "per corrispondere a" instead of "per conformarli a"). The section heading "Scala a grandi numeri di qubit" is ambiguous in Italian — "Scala" reads first as the noun "scale" rather than the imperative.

examples.source: you will scale the simple program up to utility level / utility-scale work is crucial
examples.suggested: portare il programma semplice su scala di utilità / il lavoro su scala di utilità
examples.translation: porterai il programma semplice a livello di utilità / il lavoro a scala di utilità è fondamentale
examples.why: The same term-of-art ('utility level' / 'utility-scale') is rendered two different ways in one file, and 'a livello di utilità' reads as a generic 'at the utility level' rather than the quantum-utility scale the page is teaching.

examples.source: the $n^{th}$ digit has value $1 \ll n$ or $2^n$
examples.suggested: la cifra $n$-esima ha valore $1 \ll n$ o $2^n$
examples.translation: l'$n^{th}$ cifra ha valore $1 \ll n$ o $2^n$
examples.why: The English ordinal suffix 'th' is left untranslated inside Italian prose and the article/adjective order is calqued from English; an Italian technical writer would always write 'la cifra $n$-esima'.

examples.source: The resilience level specifies how much resilience to build against errors.
examples.suggested: Il livello di resilienza indica quanta protezione dagli errori applicare.
examples.translation: Il livello di resilienza specifica quanta resilienza costruire contro gli errori.
examples.why: 'costruire resilienza contro gli errori' is a word-for-word trace of 'build resilience against'; the collocation does not exist in Italian technical prose and reads as machine output.

examples.source: transforms the circuit and observables to match that backend's ISA
examples.suggested: trasforma il circuito e gli osservabili per conformarli all'ISA di quel backend
examples.translation: trasforma il circuito e gli osservabili per corrispondere all'ISA di quel backend
examples.why: 'per corrispondere a' is a calque of 'to match'; without a reflexive/transitive object the Italian sentence makes the code (not the circuit) the thing that corresponds, which is stiff and slightly ungrammatical.

examples.source: ## Scale to large numbers of qubits
examples.suggested: ## Passa a un gran numero di qubit
examples.translation: ## Scala a grandi numeri di qubit
examples.why: 'Scala' at the head of a heading parses first as the noun 'scale/ladder' rather than the imperative verb, so the reader has to re-read; the plural 'grandi numeri' is also an English-driven plural where Italian uses the singular.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no dropped caveats: the security warning ("Evita di eseguire codice su una macchina non attendibile…"), the "scade dopo al massimo un'ora" bearer-token lifetime, and the "cambia la tua chiave API dopo ogni utilizzo" instruction all match the English exactly, and the informal "tu" register (Segui, Evita, Proteggi, Autentica, Passa il cursore) holds without a single Lei slip. Terminology is consistent and idiomatic: "chiave API"/"token API", "bearer token" and "CRN" correctly left in English, "ambiente non attendibile" used uniformly for "untrusted environment". The one thing a native technical editor would rewrite is the opening of the REST section (line 50), which stacks two final "per" clauses in a calqued English word order: "Segui questi passaggi per utilizzare la tua chiave API direttamente per autenticarti all'API REST di Qiskit Runtime". Nothing here misleads a learner.

examples.source: Follow these steps to use your API key directly to authenticate to the Qiskit Runtime REST API, where `<your_API_KEY>` is the 44-character API key…
examples.suggested: Segui questi passaggi per autenticarti all'API REST di Qiskit Runtime usando direttamente la tua chiave API, dove `<your_API_KEY>` è la chiave API a 44 caratteri…
examples.translation: Segui questi passaggi per utilizzare la tua chiave API direttamente per autenticarti all'API REST di Qiskit Runtime, dove `<your_API_KEY>` è la chiave API a 44 caratteri…
examples.why: Two chained purpose clauses ('per utilizzare … per autenticarti') mirror the English infinitive stacking; Italian technical prose puts the goal first and the means in a gerund, so the sentence currently reads as fluent MT rather than native writing. Meaning is unaffected.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout and the hard concepts land correctly (variational→変分, parameterized→パラメーター化, unitary coupled-cluster→ユニタリー結合クラスター試行状態, shots→ショット, in-place addition and the A=2/B=3 adder example all match the English), and register is consistent plain desu/masu with no keigo. The main defects are terminological and cosmetic: "transpiling" in the quantum-volume paragraph is flattened to a generic 変換 and re-attached to 結果 ("結果を変換・後処理するソフトウェアスタック"), which loses the トランスパイル concept and implies the stack converts the results rather than the circuits; and "gate" is rendered two ways inside a single sentence (「単一Qubitゲートや2-Qubit Gateから組み立てる…多Qubit Gate」). Readability also suffers from missing word boundaries where the kept-English glossary terms collide — 単一QubitRotation Gate, 単一QubitGate — which a native technical editor would space or hyphenate. Two small qualifiers are dropped: "certain diagonal gates" becomes plain 対角なGate, and the hedge "These may be useful with algorithms such as…" is hardened to 役立ちます.

examples.source: including qubit count, instruction fidelity, qubit connectivity, and the software stack transpiling and post-processing results
examples.suggested: Qubit数、命令忠実度、Qubit間の接続性、そしてCircuitのトランスパイルと結果の後処理を担うソフトウェアスタックを含む、コンピューターのすべての側面が考慮されます。
examples.translation: Qubit数、命令忠実度、Qubit間の接続性、そして結果を変換・後処理するソフトウェアスタックを含む、コンピューターのすべての側面が考慮されます。
examples.why: 'transpiling' is a core Qiskit term and is flattened to the generic 変換, then bound to 結果 — so the sentence says the stack converts the *results*, whereas transpilation acts on the circuit. The concept the learner should pick up (compiling circuits to hardware) disappears.

examples.source: others are multi-qubit gates that usually need building from single- and two-qubit gates
examples.suggested: 通常は単一Qubit Gateや2-Qubit Gateから組み立てる必要がある多Qubit Gateもあります
examples.translation: 通常は単一Qubitゲートや2-Qubit Gateから組み立てる必要がある多Qubit Gateもあります
examples.why: 'gate' appears as both katakana ゲート and English Gate inside one sentence; the file otherwise uses Gate consistently (標準Gate, Hadamard Gate, エンタングリング Gate). Pick one rendering.

examples.source: These circuits alternate layers of single-qubit rotation gates with layers of multi-qubit entangling gates. / blocks of parameterized single-qubit gates
examples.suggested: 単一Qubitの回転Gateの層と、多Qubitのエンタングリング Gateの層を交互に配置します / パラメーター化された単一Qubit Gateのブロック
examples.translation: 単一QubitRotation Gateの層と多Qubitエンタングリング Gateの層を交互に配置します / パラメーター化された単一QubitGateのブロック
examples.why: Kept-English glossary terms run together with no separator (単一QubitRotation Gate, 単一QubitGate), producing strings no Japanese technical writer would set that way; spacing or a の particle is needed for the phrase to parse at reading speed.

examples.source: These circuits sandwich certain diagonal gates (in the computational basis) between blocks of Hadamard gates.
examples.suggested: これらのCircuitは、計算基底において対角な特定のGateをHadamard Gateのブロックで挟み込みます。
examples.translation: これらのCircuitは、計算基底において対角なGateをHadamard Gateのブロックでサンドイッチ状に挟みます。
examples.why: 'certain' is dropped, so the Japanese reads as though *all* diagonal gates are used rather than a particular family — a small but real over-generalization in a definitional sentence.

examples.source: These may be useful with algorithms such as amplitude estimation for finance applications, and in algorithms like the HHL algorithm
examples.suggested: これらは、金融アプリケーション向けの振幅推定アルゴリズムや、線形方程式系を解くHHLアルゴリズムなどで役立つ場合があります。
examples.translation: これらは、金融アプリケーション向けの振幅推定アルゴリズムや、線形方程式系を解くHHLアルゴリズムなどに役立ちます。
examples.why: The English hedge 'may be useful' is hardened into a flat assertion 役立ちます, slightly overstating how established these applications are.

editor_note: No misleading content: the load-bearing physics passages are faithful — the betas-too-small explanation (「ベータ値が小さすぎて、後続のコスト関数において最小固有状態にペナルティを与えられなかった」), the "no variational calculation can go below the true ground state" argument, and the final caveat 「重なりペナルティがどれほど適切でも、真の基底状態の良い推定値が得られていなければ…」 all carry the English meaning intact. The defects are consistency and polish: "observable" is split between オブザーバブル (6×) and 観測量 (4×) — the same operator $\hat O_2$ is 観測量 at §VQD but オブザーバブル in the chemistry section; "circuit" is split between the English "Circuit" (26×) and 回路 (4×, e.g. 量子回路 / 重なり回路); "transpile" alternates Transpile (3×) and トランスパイル (2×); "iterations" alternates イテレーション and 反復回数; and 「Qiskitパターンフレームワーク」 (line 21) becomes 「Qiskit パターンズフレームワーク」 (line 394). Smaller items: 「コスト関数の景観」 is a calque of "landscape" (native usage is ランドスケープ/地形), 「重なり積分」 over-translates a plain "overlap calculation" that is done with fidelity circuits, not an integral, and 「ご覧のとおり」 (line 200) is a 尊敬語 slip against the desu/masu-no-keigo convention.

examples.source: the eigenvalue of the following observable / the lowest eigenvalue of our observables / the observable representing energy
examples.suggested: Pick one and use it throughout — オブザーバブル (matches the Qiskit-JA house style used elsewhere in this course).
examples.translation: 以下のオブザーバブルの固有値 … 観測量の最小固有値 … エネルギーを表すオブザーバブル
examples.why: The same concept is rendered two ways in one file (オブザーバブル 6×, 観測量 4×); a learner meeting 観測量 in the VQD section may not connect it to the オブザーバブル introduced at the top.

examples.source: Consider the following circuit. … we must optimize the quantum circuits … (using the overlap circuits and penalty terms)
examples.suggested: Use one convention for circuit — either the English "Circuit" everywhere or 回路 everywhere (e.g. 重なり Circuit / 量子 Circuit).
examples.translation: 次のCircuitを考えます。… 量子回路を最適化する必要があります … （重なり回路とペナルティ項を使用）
examples.why: "Circuit" appears 26× untranslated while 回路 appears 4× for the identical concept, sometimes within adjacent paragraphs.

examples.source: an optimizer designed for non-smooth cost function landscapes usually does better
examples.suggested: 滑らかでないコスト関数のランドスケープに適したオプティマイザーのほうが、通常は良い結果を出します
examples.translation: 滑らかでないコスト関数の景観に対応したオプティマイザーが通常より良い結果を出します
examples.why: 景観 is a literal calque (it means scenery/streetscape); Japanese quantum-optimization writing uses ランドスケープ (or 地形) for a cost landscape, so the current wording reads as machine translation.

examples.source: We'll add our overlap calculation:
examples.suggested: 重なりの計算を追加します。
examples.translation: 重なり積分の計算を追加します。
examples.why: 積分 (integral) is added by the translator; the overlap here is estimated by a fidelity/ComputeUncompute circuit, not by evaluating an integral, so the chemistry term over-specifies the method.

examples.source: As you can see, the result is extremely close to the ideal.
examples.suggested: 見てのとおり、結果は理想値に非常に近い値になっています。
examples.translation: ご覧のとおり、結果は理想値に非常に近い値になっています。
examples.why: ご覧 is 尊敬語 and breaks the file's otherwise consistent plain desu/masu register (single occurrence; the rest of the file holds the convention).

examples.source: the Qiskit patterns framework … Here we implement the Qiskit patterns framework, explicitly.
examples.suggested: Qiskit パターン フレームワーク (one spelling, with consistent spacing)
examples.translation: Qiskitパターンフレームワーク … Qiskit パターンズフレームワーク
examples.why: The product name is spelled two different ways (パターン vs パターンズ, and with/without the space after Qiskit) in the same document.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the counterfactual in "목표 Circuit에 넉넉한 수의 Trotter 단계를 사용하지 않았다면 사용하게 되었을 Circuit", the stopping-point sentence ("AQC를 사용하지 않았을 때 비교 Circuit이 도달했을 값 이상이 되도록…"), and the fidelity/Trotter-error claims all match the English exactly, and core terms are correct and consistent (observable→관측량, fidelity→충실도, MPS→행렬곱 상태, ansatz/Hamiltonian/Circuit/Backend/Transpile kept English per the ko corpus convention). The one real terminology blemish is the hybrid "tensor 네트워크" (lines 13, 19, 83, 174, 176) — half English, half Korean; the corpus uses 텐서 (171 hits) and this file holds all 5 corpus occurrences of the hybrid form, and it sits inconsistently beside the fully-translated 행렬곱 상태 in the very same sentence (line 176). Two prose spots are stiff calques of the English word order: the noun pile "$t_i=0$에서 $t_f=4$까지 발전의 AQC 부분에 대한 "목표" Circuit" (line 83) and "상수 배 만큼만 영향을 주므로" (line 83, also mis-spaced; should be 상수 배만큼만). Nothing here would mislead a learner; the 합니다체 register matches the rest of the ko corpus (8428 vs 50) and is not counted as a defect.

examples.source: target tensor-network state / tensor network simulator
examples.suggested: 목표 텐서 네트워크 상태 / 텐서 네트워크 시뮬레이터
examples.translation: 목표 tensor 네트워크 상태 / tensor 네트워크 시뮬레이터
examples.why: Half-transliterated hybrid a Korean technical writer would not write; the corpus standard is 텐서 (171 uses) and the same sentence already translates MPS as 행렬곱 상태, so the keep-English policy is applied inconsistently. Lowercase 'tensor' also opens the heading on line 174.

examples.source: A "target" circuit for the AQC portion of the evolution, from $t_i=0$ to $t_f=4$.
examples.suggested: 시간 발전 중 AQC가 담당하는 $t_i=0$부터 $t_f=4$까지 구간의 "목표" Circuit.
examples.translation: $t_i=0$에서 $t_f=4$까지 발전의 AQC 부분에 대한 "목표" Circuit.
examples.why: Calqued English noun stacking: '발전의 AQC 부분에 대한' forces two genitive links in a row and reads as MT. Native phrasing puts the AQC portion in a relative clause.

examples.source: the number of layers affects execution time only by a constant factor
examples.suggested: 레이어 수를 늘려도 실행 시간은 상수 배만큼만 늘어나므로
examples.translation: 레이어 수는 실행 시간에 상수 배 만큼만 영향을 주므로
examples.why: '…에 상수 배 만큼만 영향을 주다' is a literal rendering of 'affects … by a constant factor' that is stiff in Korean, and 배 is a bound noun so '상수 배 만큼만' is mis-spaced (상수 배만큼만).

editor_note: No misleading content: the math walkthroughs, the constant/balanced promise, the little-endian note, the 2^n/2+1 worst case, and the "exponential over deterministic, no speedup over probabilistic" caveat all survive intact. But an editor would fix several things. (1) "phase kickback" is rendered three different ways in one file — 위상 역전(phase-kickback) at first introduction (~L309), 위상 반작용 in the D-J and B-V sections (~L385, L573, L591), and 위상 반동 in the unglossed summary bullets and short-answer question (~L704, L721); 위상 역전 ("phase inversion") is also the weakest of the three. (2) An untranslated English word is left sitting in Korean prose: "그 개선은 modest했습니다" (~L379). (3) Two section headings were never translated ("## The Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm" ~L377, "### The Bernstein - Vazirani problem" ~L551), and the algorithm's own name splits between 도이치/도이치-요자 in the intro and Latin "Deutsch"/"Deutsch-Jozsa" from L234 on; "query" likewise splits between 쿼리 (L252–256) and 질의 (L445, L530, L690). (4) Core terms are left in capitalized Latin script inside Korean sentences — "Qubit 0은", "양자 Circuit", "$U_f$ Gate", "Transpile된 Circuit" — where a Korean quantum engineer would write 큐비트, 회로, 게이트, 트랜스파일; casing even flips within one sentence (qubit vs Qubit).

examples.source: This is known as the "phase-kickback" phenomenon … the phase-kickback allows one to read out the state of qubit 0 … the phase kickback mechanism is a counterintuitive quantum phenomena
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering and use it everywhere — e.g. 위상 킥백(phase kickback), glossed once at first use.
examples.translation: 이를 "위상 역전(phase-kickback)" 현상이라고 하며 … 위상 반작용(phase-kickback)을 통해 qubit 0의 상태를 읽어 … 위상 반동 메커니즘은 … 직관에 반하는 양자 현상입니다
examples.why: The file's single most important named mechanism appears under three different Korean names; the first-use rendering 위상 역전 ("phase inversion") is also the least accurate, and the summary bullets use 위상 반동 with no English gloss to reconnect it.

examples.source: it was only a modest improvement: it required just one query, compared to two in the classical case
examples.suggested: 그 개선은 크지 않았습니다. 고전적인 경우의 두 번에 비해 단 한 번의 질의만 필요했으니까요.
examples.translation: 그 개선은 modest했습니다. 고전적인 경우의 두 번에 비해 단 한 번의 질의만 필요했습니다
examples.why: An English adjective is left untranslated and inflected as Korean ("modest했습니다") — an obvious raw-MT artifact no Korean technical writer would produce.

examples.source: ## The Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm / ### The Bernstein - Vazirani problem
examples.suggested: ## 도이치-요자 알고리즘 / ### 번스타인-바지라니 문제
examples.translation: ## The Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm / ### The Bernstein - Vazirani problem
examples.why: Two section headings were skipped entirely while every other heading (소개, 문제, 알고리즘, 결론, 이해도 확인) is translated — the reader hits English mid-document.

examples.source: while a quantum circuit might be able to evaluate multiple input states … We can learn about the function with the following gate … we need to optimize and transpile the circuit
examples.suggested: 양자 회로가 … 다음 게이트를 사용하여 … 회로를 최적화하고 트랜스파일해야 합니다
examples.translation: 양자 Circuit이 여러 입력 상태를 동시에 평가할 수 있다 하더라도 … 다음 Gate를 사용하여 함수에 대해 알아볼 수 있습니다 … Circuit을 … 최적화하고 Transpile해야 합니다
examples.why: Everyday domain nouns are left in capitalized Latin script inside Korean prose, and the casing is inconsistent even within a sentence ("Qubit 0은 $x$가 무엇인지, qubit 1은…"); Korean Qiskit docs conventionally use 큐비트/회로/게이트.

examples.source: While quantum parallelism alone doesn't give us an advantage over classical computers, we can pair this with another quantum phenomena, interference, to achieve a speed-up.
examples.suggested: 양자 병렬성만으로는 고전 컴퓨터에 비해 아무런 이점도 얻을 수 없지만, …
examples.translation: 양자 병렬성만으로는 고전 컴퓨터에 비해 이점을 얻기 어렵지만, 이를 또 다른 양자 현상인 간섭(interference)과 결합하면 속도 향상을 달성할 수 있습니다.
examples.why: The English states flatly that parallelism alone gives no advantage — the whole point the preceding section just established. "얻기 어렵지만" ("is hard to obtain") softens a categorical claim into a difficulty, weakening the lesson's takeaway.

examples.source: There are four possible binary functions taking a single bit to another single bit
examples.suggested: 단일 비트를 다른 단일 비트로 대응시키는 이진 함수는 네 가지가 있습니다
examples.translation: 단일 비트를 다른 단일 비트로 취하는 이진 함수는 네 가지가 있습니다
examples.why: "…로 취하는" is a word-for-word calque of "taking … to …" and is not idiomatic Korean; the same English phrase is correctly rendered as "단일 비트를 단일 비트로 매핑하는" at L242, so the file contradicts itself.

examples.source: Hopefully this simplest case gives you a sense for how the general case with $n$ qubits works
examples.suggested: 이 가장 단순한 경우를 통해 $n$개 큐비트의 일반적인 경우가 어떻게 작동하는지 감을 잡으셨기를 바랍니다
examples.translation: 이 가장 단순한 경우가 $n$개의 Qubit으로 된 일반적인 경우가 어떻게 작동하는지 직관을 줄 것입니다
examples.why: The teacher's hedge ("Hopefully…") becomes a flat assertion that the reader will get the intuition; the warm, inviting register of the worked answer flattens into a claim about the reader.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, swapped quantities or dropped caveats — but a native technical editor would change several things. The worst is "the four CHSH correlators" rendered as "empat perekat CHSH" ("perekat" = glue/adhesive, not correlator; it should be "pengkorelasi"/"korelator"), and "we tile the backend" rendered with the non-word "merubin" (tile = "jubin", so "menjubin"; a native writer would simply say "kita memenuhi/mengisi backend dengan..."). Terminology is also unstable in casing and language mix: "Circuit" is kept in English and capitalized mid-sentence ("membina Circuit Bell-state CHSH berparameter", "sub-Circuit CHSH", "satu Circuit yang lebih besar") while "litar" never appears, and "backend" alternates between lowercase ("model hingar backend", "backend yang kamu pilih") and capitalized "Backend" ("kita merubin Backend", "Backend mengekalkan keterjaitan"); entanglement likewise splits roots between "keterjaitan" (noun) and "terjalin" (adjective, "foton terjalin", "pasangan terjalin"). Smaller: "observable" as the bare nominal "boleh ukur" ("pelbagai boleh ukur") is stiff, "shows that" is strengthened to "membuktikan" (proves) twice, "hand-picked" is calqued as "dipilih tangan", "unambiguous" uses the wrong idiom "tidak berbelah bahagi" (normally loyalty, not clarity), and the file uses casual "kamu" rather than "anda" throughout.

examples.source: the four CHSH correlators map to the Pauli operators $ZZ$, $ZX$, $XZ$, and $XX$
examples.suggested: empat pengkorelasi (korelator) CHSH dipetakan kepada operator Pauli ...
examples.translation: empat perekat CHSH dipetakan kepada operator Pauli $ZZ$, $ZX$, $XZ$, dan $XX$
examples.why: "perekat" means glue/adhesive and has no relation to correlation; the reader gets an opaque non-term where the English names a well-defined quantity.

examples.source: Here we tile the backend with as many disjoint Bell pairs as its connectivity allows
examples.suggested: Di sini kita memenuhi backend dengan seberapa banyak pasangan Bell tidak bertindih yang dibenarkan oleh ketersambungannya
examples.translation: Di sini kita merubin Backend dengan seberapa banyak pasangan Bell yang tidak bertindih seperti yang dibenarkan oleh ketersambungannya
examples.why: "merubin" is not a Malay word (tile = "jubin" → "menjubin"), and the capitalized "Backend" clashes with lowercase "backend" used elsewhere in the same file.

examples.source: parameterized Bell-state CHSH circuit / We write the CHSH circuit / one circuit bigger
examples.suggested: litar CHSH berparameter (or lowercase, consistently, if the keep-English convention is intended)
examples.translation: Circuit Bell-state CHSH berparameter / Kita menulis Circuit CHSH / satu Circuit yang lebih besar
examples.why: "Circuit" is kept in English and capitalized mid-sentence at every occurrence while every other domain noun is translated; it reads as a glossary artifact, not an editorial decision.

examples.source: Demonstrating a violation of the CHSH inequality shows that quantum mechanics is incompatible with local hidden-variable theories
examples.suggested: ... menunjukkan bahawa mekanik kuantum tidak serasi dengan ...
examples.translation: Menunjukkan pelanggaran ketaksamaan CHSH membuktikan bahawa mekanik kuantum tidak serasi dengan teori pembolehubah tersembunyi setempat
examples.why: "membuktikan" (proves) is stronger than the English "shows"; the same strengthening recurs at the end of the Background section ("membuktikan bahawa" for "so quantum mechanics is not compatible").

examples.source: rather than a single hand-picked pair / not just on a single hand-picked pair ... the conclusion is unambiguous
examples.suggested: ... satu pasangan yang dipilih secara manual/khas ... kesimpulannya jelas dan tidak boleh disangkal
examples.translation: daripada satu pasangan yang dipilih tangan / bukan hanya pada satu pasangan yang dipilih tangan ... kesimpulannya tidak berbelah bahagi
examples.why: "dipilih tangan" is a word-for-word calque of "hand-picked", and "tidak berbelah bahagi" is an idiom about undivided loyalty, not about an unambiguous conclusion.

editor_note: Faithful and technically accurate throughout: no semantic drift, informal "tu" holds consistently ("devi decidere", "Scegli questo", "Consulta", "Dai un'occhiata"), and domain terms are correct and stable (transpiler/pass manager/coupling map/basis gate/entry point kept in English; "sintesi unitaria", "sintesi ad alto livello", "operatore di Clifford", "qubit", "pass di transpilazione"). Three things a native technical editor would still change: "Backend" is capitalized mid-sentence twice ("informazioni sul Backend di destinazione", "specifica il Backend di destinazione") — a glossary artifact, Italian lowercases it, and it clashes with the lowercase "target"/"coupling map" alongside it; "un circuito quantistico che implementa quella unitaria" uses "unitaria" as a bare noun, which is not idiomatic Italian (and would elide to "quell'unitaria" anyway) where "quella matrice unitaria" is the natural rendering; and "un pass manager che può essere sostituito a una delle 6 fasi" is a stiff literary construction that reads ambiguously to modern readers. Also, the "also" in "whose names are also reserved" is dropped ("i cui nomi sono riservati"), losing the link back to the uniqueness requirement — harmless but a lost connective.

examples.source: The PassManagerConfig object stores information about the target backend, such as its coupling map and basis gates. / `target` specifies the target backend
examples.suggested: ... informazioni sul backend di destinazione ... / `target` specifica il backend di destinazione
examples.translation: L'oggetto PassManagerConfig memorizza informazioni sul Backend di destinazione, come la sua coupling map e i basis gate. / `target` specifica il Backend di destinazione
examples.why: "Backend" is a common noun in Italian and is not capitalized mid-sentence; the capital B reads as a glossary/term-list artifact and is inconsistent with the lowercase "coupling map", "basis gate" and "target" used in the same sentences.

examples.source: outputs a description of a quantum circuit implementing that unitary
examples.suggested: produce come output la descrizione di un circuito quantistico che implementa quella matrice unitaria
examples.translation: produce come output la descrizione di un circuito quantistico che implementa quella unitaria
examples.why: English nominalizes "unitary"; Italian does not use "unitaria" as a bare noun in technical prose (and it would elide to "quell'unitaria"). A native writer repeats the head noun "matrice", especially since the same sentence already introduced "una matrice unitaria".

examples.source: Choose this if you are defining a pass manager that can be substituted for one of the 6 stages of a preset staged pass manager.
examples.suggested: Scegli questo se stai definendo un pass manager che può sostituire una delle 6 fasi di un preset staged pass manager.
examples.translation: Scegli questo se stai definendo un pass manager che può essere sostituito a una delle 6 fasi di un preset staged pass manager.
examples.why: "essere sostituito a X" is a literary construction that most readers parse ambiguously (it can be misread as "replaced by X"); the active "può sostituire una delle 6 fasi" states the intended direction unambiguously and is what a technical writer would use.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inversion, dropped caveat or altered quantity; the approximation-degree, seed and initial-layout explanations all teach what the English teaches (0.0 = penghampiran maksimum, 1.0 lalai; qubit 5/qubit 6 mapping intact; isipadu kuantum is the right term). The defects are surface-level. (1) "Circuit" is left in capitalised English everywhere ("Circuit kuantum", "Circuit hasil", "Circuit output dari sintesis") where a Malay technical writer writes "litar", while "gate" IS translated as "get" — an inconsistent keep-English policy, and line 44 then slips back to English "gate" ("kaedah sintesis gate mana"), splitting get/gate within one file. (2) In the seed section the English noun "runs" is rendered as the imperative verb "jalankan": "jadi jalankan transpilasi berulang mungkin mengembalikan keputusan yang berbeza" and "Jalankan berulang menggunakan benih yang sama akan mengembalikan..." — ungrammatical raw-MT syntax; "larian transpilasi berulang" / "Larian berulang" is the native form. (3) Compiler "pass" is rendered "laluan" (= path/route), giving "Laluan pemilihan susun atur" and "Nama laluan penghalaan" — recognisable but the literal wrong sense. (4) Assorted stiffness: the "di mana" relative calque, Backend/backend capitalisation flip-flop, and a missing "kepadanya" in the $i$-th element sentence.

examples.source: Some parts of the transpiler are stochastic, so repeated transpilation runs may return different results. ... Repeated runs using the same seed will return the same results.
examples.suggested: ... jadi larian transpilasi berulang mungkin mengembalikan keputusan yang berbeza. ... Larian berulang menggunakan benih yang sama akan mengembalikan keputusan yang sama.
examples.translation: Beberapa bahagian Transpiler adalah stokastik, jadi jalankan transpilasi berulang mungkin mengembalikan keputusan yang berbeza. ... Jalankan berulang menggunakan benih yang sama akan mengembalikan keputusan yang sama.
examples.why: The English noun "runs" is translated as the imperative verb "jalankan", so the clause has an imperative where its subject should be — ungrammatical in Malay and unmistakably machine syntax. "Larian" is the noun a native technical writer uses.

examples.source: We must also specify the `basis_gates` to let the synthesis method know which gates it can use for the approximate synthesis.
examples.suggested: ... untuk memberitahu kaedah sintesis get mana yang boleh digunakannya ...
examples.translation: Kami juga mesti menentukan `basis_gates` untuk memberitahu kaedah sintesis gate mana yang boleh digunakannya untuk sintesis penghampiran.
examples.why: Every other occurrence in the file translates gate as "get" ("get CX", "get diskret", "get swap"); here it reverts to English "gate", splitting the term within a single file.

examples.source: the resultant circuit ... the output circuit from synthesis ... the qubits contained in your circuit
examples.suggested: litar hasil ... litar output daripada sintesis ... qubit yang terkandung dalam litar anda
examples.translation: Circuit hasil ... Circuit output dari sintesis ... qubit yang terkandung dalam Circuit anda
examples.why: "Circuit" is kept in English and capitalised mid-sentence throughout, which reads as an unresolved glossary leak rather than a deliberate convention — especially next to fully translated "get", "penghampiran" and "susun atur". "Litar (kuantum)" is the established Malay term.

examples.source: The layout selection pass ... Name of routing pass ... Name of scheduling pass
examples.suggested: Pass pemilihan susun atur ... Nama pass penghalaan ... Nama pass penjadualan
examples.translation: Laluan pemilihan susun atur ... Nama laluan penghalaan ... Nama laluan penjadualan
examples.why: A transpiler "pass" is a compilation stage, not a route; "laluan" means path/passage, so "laluan penghalaan" reads as "routing path". Recognisable in context, but it is the literal-wrong sense of the word.

editor_note: Overall fluent, faithful and correctly informal ("você"); domain/product terms (QPU, job, instância, segundos de runtime, limite de custo) are handled sensibly. Three things a native technical editor would change. (1) In the spending-notifications list, "billing system" and "invoicing system" are both rendered "sistema de faturamento", collapsing the EN distinction into a circular sentence — "O sistema de faturamento pode levar vários dias para enviar informações ao sistema de faturamento"; "sistema de emissão de faturas/cobrança" would restore it. (2) "workload" is rendered "carga de trabalho" in the intro and the cost-limit definition but left as English "workload" in the "Visualizar uso do workload" section — same concept, two renderings in one file. (3) UI strings are handled inconsistently: **Edit details**, **Save changes**, **Instance usage**, **Total workloads (all types)** stay English (matching the product UI), yet the job-status strings are translated ("Cancelado", "Executou por tempo excessivo"), so a reader looking for "Canceled / Ran too long" in the console will not find those labels. None of these teach a wrong concept.

examples.source: The billing system can take multiple days to get information to the invoicing system, which might cause further delay in notifications.
examples.suggested: O sistema de cobrança pode levar vários dias para enviar informações ao sistema de emissão de faturas, o que pode causar atrasos adicionais nas notificações.
examples.translation: O sistema de faturamento pode levar vários dias para enviar informações ao sistema de faturamento, o que pode causar atrasos adicionais nas notificações.
examples.why: "billing system" and "invoicing system" are two different systems in the EN; both became "sistema de faturamento", so the sentence now says a system sends information to itself — the causal chain behind the notification delay is lost.

examples.source: ### View workload usage / To determine how much has been billed to each workload associated with an instance
examples.suggested: ### Visualizar uso da carga de trabalho / ... quanto foi cobrado de cada carga de trabalho associada a uma instância
examples.translation: ### Visualizar uso do workload / Para determinar quanto foi cobrado de cada workload associado a uma instância
examples.why: The same term is "carga de trabalho" in the intro and in the _limite de custo_ definition (lines 11 and 13) but English "workload" here; pick one rendering for the file.

examples.source: Its status is set to Canceled with a reason of Ran too long.
examples.suggested: Seu status é definido como Canceled, com o motivo Ran too long (executou por tempo excessivo).
examples.translation: Seu status é definido como Cancelado com o motivo "Executou por tempo excessivo".
examples.why: Every other product-UI label in the file is deliberately left in English (**Edit details**, **Save changes**, **Instance usage**, **Total workloads (all types)**); translating these two status strings breaks that convention and hides the literal text the user will see in the console.

examples.source: the cost for X runtime seconds might be different when initially calculated in USD than when you’re actually charged in your local currency
examples.suggested: o custo de X segundos de runtime calculado inicialmente em USD pode ser diferente do valor efetivamente cobrado na sua moeda local
examples.translation: o custo por X segundos de runtime pode ser diferente quando calculado inicialmente em USD e quando você é efetivamente cobrado na sua moeda local
examples.why: The English comparative "different ... than" is calqued as "diferente ... e", which reads as an incomplete comparison in Portuguese; the contrast between the two amounts is blurred.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, all criteria numbers, the 2% readout error, the 127-qubit/T1-T2 facts and the "P(qubit=1) diminuisce" pedagogy match the English — and the informal "tu" register holds consistently ("Eseguirai", "Dovresti vedere", "Completa il codice"). The defect is a glossary-leak pattern: the English noun "Circuit" is left untranslated and capitalized in eight places ("Eseguirai Circuit su simulatori", "costruire Circuit più grandi", "per ciascun Circuit", "a metà Circuit", "Esegui il transpiling dei Circuit", "lo stesso Circuit", "costruire Circuit su più qubit") while the rest of the file correctly says "circuito/circuiti" — the same file, two renderings of the same term. The same artifact hits "Backend" (capitalized in "le proprietà di un Backend IBM", "un Backend fittizio", "del Backend `FakeBrisbane`" but lowercase "per questo backend" two lines later), "multi-Qubit" (capital Q against lowercase "qubit" everywhere else), and the mid-sentence lowercase "gate" inside title-case headings ("Set Universale di gate Quantistici", "**gate Universali**"). "transpile" is also split three ways — "il transpiling", "traspilato", "traspilare". Two smaller calques: "sui dispositivi quantum IBM" (should be "quantistici") and "sistemi ripetitori" for "repeater systems" ("ripetitori quantistici"). None of this misleads a learner; all of it is what a native technical editor would fix.

examples.source: You will get to run circuits on simulators and real IBM Quantum devices
examples.suggested: Eseguirai circuiti su simulatori e su veri dispositivi IBM Quantum
examples.translation: Eseguirai Circuit su simulatori e veri dispositivi IBM Quantum
examples.why: The English noun 'circuit' is left untranslated and capitalized as 'Circuit' in eight places, while the same file elsewhere uses the correct 'circuito/circuiti' (e.g. 'i circuiti GHZ', 'la profondità del circuito'). Same term, two renderings within one file — a glossary-substitution artifact, not a translation choice.

examples.source: we can take an IBM backend's properties … Transpile the circuits for this backend
examples.suggested: le proprietà di un backend IBM … Esegui il transpiling dei circuiti per questo backend
examples.translation: possiamo prendere le proprietà di un Backend IBM … Esegui il transpiling dei Circuit per questo backend
examples.why: 'backend' (correctly kept in English) is capitalized as a proper noun in five places but lowercase in others, sometimes within the same sentence pair. Inconsistent casing of a domain term inside one file.

examples.source: any multi-qubit unitary can be composed from 1- and 2-qubit gates
examples.suggested: qualsiasi unitaria multi-qubit può essere composta da gate a 1 e 2 qubit
examples.translation: qualsiasi unitaria multi-Qubit può essere composta da gate a 1 e 2 qubit
examples.why: 'multi-Qubit' with a capital Q contradicts the lowercase 'qubit' used consistently everywhere else in the file, including in the same sentence.

examples.source: Transpile the circuits for this backend and execute them.
examples.suggested: Traspila i circuiti per questo backend ed eseguili.
examples.translation: Esegui il transpiling dei Circuit per questo backend ed eseguili.
examples.why: 'Esegui … ed eseguili' repeats the same verb twice in one short imperative, and 'il transpiling' is a third rendering of a verb the file elsewhere writes as 'traspilare' (line ~511) and 'traspilato' (line ~415). A native technical writer would pick one form.

examples.source: In practice, on IBM quantum devices each qubit is automatically reset to |0〉
examples.suggested: In pratica, sui dispositivi quantistici IBM ogni qubit viene automaticamente reimpostato a |0〉
examples.translation: In pratica, sui dispositivi quantum IBM ogni qubit viene automaticamente reimpostato a |0〉
examples.why: The English adjective 'quantum' is carried over untranslated as a bare adjective, a calque; Italian technical prose says 'dispositivi quantistici' — which the same file uses correctly elsewhere ('computer quantistico', 'hardware quantistica').

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no inverted claims, no dropped caveats — but two terminology habits a Korean editor would change. (1) "circuit" and "gate" are left as capitalized English mid-sentence everywhere ("양자 Circuit", "Circuit 구축 도구", "Circuit, 명령어, Gate"), even though every neighboring term IS translated (레지스터, 명령어, 연산자, 파라미터) and the project's own translation/glossary/ko.json lists "Circuit"/"Gate" as English leaks with preferred 회로/게이트; it is internally consistent, so not misleading, just jarringly un-Korean. (2) "input observables" becomes "입력 관측값" (observed values, a number) where the operator sense wants 관측 가능량/관측량 — recognizable but the wrong sense of the word. Two calques also read as MT rather than native prose: "수정된 측정 확률을 해결하는" for "solves for corrected measurement probabilities" (해결 = solve a problem; Korean wants 구하는/계산하는) and "Transpiler 처리 속도" using the noun Transpiler as a verb for "transpiling" (트랜스파일 속도). Register is consistent 합니다체 declaratives with 해요체 imperatives (…하세요) — the standard Korean docs convention, not honorific/드리 forms.

examples.source: quantum circuits, operators, and primitives / registers, circuits, instructions, gates, parameters
examples.suggested: 양자 회로, 연산자, 프리미티브 / 레지스터, 회로, 명령어, 게이트, 파라미터
examples.translation: 양자 Circuit, 연산자, 프리미티브 / 레지스터, Circuit, 명령어, Gate, 파라미터
examples.why: 'circuit' and 'gate' are the two most basic terms on the page and are left as capitalized English while every term beside them is translated; ko.json marks exactly these strings as leaks with preferred 회로/게이트. Consistent, so not misleading, but no Korean technical writer would write '양자 Circuit'.

examples.source: Use this module to specify input observables and analyze fidelity of outputs from primitives queries.
examples.suggested: 이 모듈을 사용하여 입력 관측 가능량(옵저버블)을 지정하고 …
examples.translation: 이 모듈을 사용하여 입력 관측값을 지정하고 프리미티브 쿼리 출력의 충실도를 분석하세요.
examples.why: 관측값 means an observed/measured value; an observable here is the operator you hand to the Estimator. Recognizable, but it nudges the learner toward 'a number you input' rather than 'an operator'. 충실도 for fidelity is correct.

examples.source: a measurement mitigation technique that solves for corrected measurement probabilities using a dimensionality reduction step …
examples.suggested: … 보정된 측정 확률을 구하는(계산하는) 측정 완화 기법 …
examples.translation: … 수정된 측정 확률을 해결하는 측정 완화 기법인 M3 …
examples.why: '확률을 해결하다' is a literal calque of 'solve for'; 해결하다 takes problems, not probabilities. Korean uses 구하다/계산하다. Also 수정된 → 보정된 is the conventional word for 'corrected' measurement data.

examples.source: the speed and quality of building, manipulating, and transpiling circuits / options for transpilation
examples.suggested: 회로 구축·조작·트랜스파일의 속도와 품질 / 다양한 트랜스파일 옵션
examples.translation: Circuit 구축, 조작 및 Transpiler 처리 속도와 품질 / 다양한 Transpiler 처리 옵션
examples.why: 'Transpiler 처리' presses the English noun into service as a verb; the action is 트랜스파일(링). Reads as machine output, and the scoping of 속도와 품질 across the three activities also blurs slightly.

editor_note: The prose is otherwise fluent, informal-"ty" throughout ("Załóżmy, że masz układ trzech qubitów", "nauczyłeś się"), and core terms are right and consistent (stan referencyjny, operator unitarny, splątanie, superpozycja, bramka X / CNOT, qubit kontrolny / docelowy). Two things a native editor must change. First, "quantum circuit" is never translated: the bare English noun "Circuit" is spliced uninflected into Polish genitive phrases seven times — "na początku naszego Circuit kwantowego", "$n$-qubitowego Circuit kwantowego", "szablonów Circuit", "parametryzowanego Circuit", "Diagram Circuit" — where Polish needs "obwodu kwantowego / obwód kwantowy" (the file otherwise never uses any Polish word for circuit, so the concept is carried only by the English loan). This is a glossary leak, not a false concept, but it is the most visible defect in the file. Second, the Summary sentence drifts: EN "Our high-level variational workload looks as follows" became "Nasz ogólny wariant wariacyjny wygląda następująco" — "workload" rendered as "wariant" (variant), producing the tautological "variational variant" and risking confusion with the *forma wariacyjna* introduced in the very next paragraph; it should be "przepływ pracy / obciążenie wariacyjne". Smaller: "bramki Hadamard" lacks the genitive of the eponym ("bramki Hadamarda"), and "tunable parameters" became "sterowalnych parametrów" (controllable) rather than "strojonych/regulowanych".

examples.source: at the start of our quantum circuit / an $n$-qubit quantum circuit / template circuits / a parameterized circuit
examples.suggested: na początku naszego obwodu kwantowego / $n$-qubitowego obwodu kwantowego / szablonów obwodów / parametryzowanego obwodu
examples.translation: na początku naszego Circuit kwantowego / $n$-qubitowego Circuit kwantowego / szablonów Circuit / parametryzowanego Circuit
examples.why: The English noun 'Circuit' is left untranslated and uninflected inside Polish genitive constructions in seven prose spots; the file never once uses 'obwód kwantowy'. Grammatically broken and reads as an unresolved glossary leak rather than written Polish.

examples.source: Our high-level variational workload looks as follows:
examples.suggested: Nasz ogólny przepływ pracy (obciążenie) wariacyjny wygląda następująco:
examples.translation: Nasz ogólny wariant wariacyjny wygląda następująco:
examples.why: 'workload' became 'wariant' (variant), yielding the tautological 'variational variant'. It mislabels the whole variational workflow shown in the diagram and can be conflated with the *forma wariacyjna* (variational form) defined in the following paragraph.

examples.source: one approach is to use a Hadamard gate on qubit $0$
examples.suggested: jednym z podejść jest zastosowanie bramki Hadamarda na qubicie $0$
examples.translation: jednym z podejść jest zastosowanie bramki Hadamard na qubicie $0$
examples.why: Polish declines the eponym: 'bramka Hadamarda', genitive 'bramki Hadamarda'. The uninflected 'Hadamard' is an English calque a Polish technical writer would not leave.

examples.source: which allows for expressing multiple tunable parameters and entanglements with ease
examples.suggested: który pozwala na łatwe wyrażenie wielu strojonych (regulowanych) parametrów i splątań
examples.translation: który pozwala na łatwe wyrażenie wielu sterowalnych parametrów i splątań
examples.why: 'tunable' → 'sterowalnych' shifts the sense to 'controllable' (which in quantum context collides with control/kontrola of gates); the intended meaning is parameters that can be tuned during optimization.

editor_note: Semantically faithful throughout — I checked every quantitative and conditional claim (constante/balanceada outputs, $2^{n-1}+1$ consultas no pior caso, $2^{-k+1}$, 99,9%, "1 consulta contra n consultas", the "se e somente se $y = s$" closure) and found no drift, no inverted condition and no dropped caveat; register is consistently the textbook "nós" voice with no formal slips. The defect is a clear two-pass split: the first half is clean Portuguese ("portas Hadamard" L57/104/120, "estados da base padrão" L67/87, "fenômeno de retorno de fase" L118) while the Bernstein-Vazirani half leaks English glossary terms — "Circuit quântico" / "*Circuit de Deutsch-Jozsa*" (L233, 272, 321, 334) instead of "circuito", "Gates Hadamard" (L326, 334, 346), "phase kickback" (L340), "gate de consulta" (L443) vs "porta de consulta" elsewhere, and "base computacional" (L326) vs "base padrão". Compounding this, "porta" (feminine) is repeatedly given masculine agreement — "um porta de consulta" (L190, 241), "o porta de consulta" (L233, 272), "O porta de consulta é então aplicado" (L340) — which no native writer would produce. Also: the second Figure title is left in English ("Bernstein-Vazirani problem", L314) while the first was translated (L44), and "um argumento chamado de *teórico da informação*" (L434) is a calque of "so-called information theoretic argument" where Portuguese wants "um argumento de *teoria da informação*".

examples.source: let's refer to the quantum circuit from above … as the *Deutsch-Jozsa circuit*.
examples.suggested: vamos nos referir ao circuito quântico descrito acima … como o *circuito de Deutsch-Jozsa*.
examples.translation: vamos nos referir ao Circuit quântico descrito acima … como o *Circuit de Deutsch-Jozsa*.
examples.why: Untranslated, capitalized English 'Circuit' leaks in four places in the second half, while the first half correctly uses 'circuito quântico' (L14, 103) and even 'circuito de Deutsch-Jozsa' (L325, 432, 442, 461). The same term is rendered two ways within one file.

examples.source: the action of $n$ Hadamard gates … the first layer of Hadamard gates … the second layer of Hadamard gates
examples.suggested: a ação de $n$ portas Hadamard … a primeira camada de portas Hadamard … a segunda camada de portas Hadamard
examples.translation: a ação de $n$ Gates Hadamard … a primeira camada de Gates Hadamard … a segunda camada de Gates Hadamard
examples.why: 'gate' is left in English (and capitalized) in the Bernstein-Vazirani section, whereas the Deutsch-Jozsa section consistently uses the correct Portuguese domain term 'portas Hadamard' (L57, 104, 120). Same split hits the query gate: 'gate de consulta' (L443) vs 'porta de consulta' everywhere else.

examples.source: a quantum circuit implementing a query gate … The query gate is then performed
examples.suggested: um circuito quântico que implementa uma porta de consulta … A porta de consulta é então aplicada
examples.translation: um circuito quântico implementando um porta de consulta … O porta de consulta é então aplicado
examples.why: 'porta' is feminine in Portuguese; 'um porta' / 'o porta … aplicado' is an agreement error repeated five times that no native technical writer would produce. L233 compounds it: 'a implementação em Circuit quântico do porta de consulta' is both ungrammatical and a leak.

examples.source: through the phase kickback phenomenon
examples.suggested: por meio do fenômeno de retorno de fase (phase kickback)
examples.translation: por meio do fenômeno de phase kickback
examples.why: The same phenomenon is named 'fenômeno de retorno de fase' at L118 and left in raw English at L340. A learner reading straight through cannot tell these are the same concept; pick one convention (either is defensible) and keep it.

examples.source: This can be reasoned through a so-called *information theoretic* argument
examples.suggested: Isso pode ser justificado por meio de um argumento dito de *teoria da informação*
examples.translation: Isso pode ser demonstrado por meio de um argumento chamado de *teórico da informação*
examples.why: Calqued adjective: 'um argumento chamado de teórico da informação' reads as a word-for-word transposition of the English attributive; Portuguese takes 'argumento de teoria da informação' (or 'argumento teórico-informacional'). 'demonstrado' also slightly overstates the English 'reasoned through'.

editor_note: No semantic drift: every claim (four-qubit expectation value from two-qubit experiments, two CNOT cuts → $9^2$ sampling overhead, coefficients/phases ignored during decomposition and re-applied at reconstruction, `num_samples` controlling draws from the joint quasiprobability distribution) matches the English, and the core terminology is right and consistent — "nilai jangkaan", "taburan kuasiprobabiliti", "overhead pensampelan", "primitif `Sampler`", "observable"/"qubit"/"gate" kept in English. What a native editor would change is cosmetic-but-visible: the kept-English terms "Circuit" and "Backend" are capitalized mid-sentence throughout ("sebuah Circuit empat-qubit", "Potong Circuit dan observable", "pada satu atau lebih Backend", "Backend palsu") while the very same words appear lowercase elsewhere in the file ("circuit kuantum", "circuit cutting", "sebuah circuit kuantum") — a glossary-fixer artifact, not a Malay convention. Also: "Qiskit pattern" is over-translated to "corak Qiskit" although Qiskit Patterns is a product-name concept the field keeps in English; "Step 4: Post-process" loses the "post-" ("Langkah 4: Proses keputusan" rather than "Pasca-proses"); and "Map the hamiltonian onto a quantum circuit" is calqued as "Petakan hamiltonian ke atas sebuah circuit kuantum" ("ke atas" = physically on top of; "kepada"/"ke dalam" is the natural Malay). None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: circuit / backend
examples.suggested: Use lowercase "circuit" and "backend" consistently mid-sentence (capitalize only at sentence start)
examples.translation: "sebuah Circuit empat-qubit", "Potong Circuit dan observable", "Circuit bersaiz penuh", "Pilih sebuah Backend", "Backend palsu" — but "circuit-circuit kuantum", "circuit kuantum", "circuit cutting" lowercase
examples.why: Same kept-English term rendered two ways within one file; mid-sentence capitalization of common nouns is not a Malay convention and reads as an automated glossary substitution rather than authored prose.

examples.source: we will work through the steps of a [Qiskit pattern]
examples.suggested: kita akan mengikuti langkah-langkah sebuah [Qiskit pattern]
examples.translation: kita akan ikut langkah-langkah sebuah [corak Qiskit]
examples.why: "Qiskit Patterns" is a named framework concept the field keeps in English; "corak" (a decorative/repeating pattern) over-translates it and breaks the link to the documentation it points at. "kita akan ikut" is also a colloquial clipping of "mengikuti".

examples.source: Step 4: Post-process results / ## Step 4: Post-process
examples.suggested: Langkah 4: Pasca-proses keputusan
examples.translation: Langkah 4: Proses keputusan / ## Langkah 4: Proses Keputusan
examples.why: The "post-" prefix is dropped, so the step name reads as generic "process the results" and loses the contrast with Step 3 (execution) that the four-step Qiskit pattern structure is teaching.

examples.source: Map the hamiltonian onto a quantum circuit.
