examples.translation: Jeśli masz dwie przemieniające się obserwowalne w różnych PUBach, ale z tym samym Circuit, nie zostaną one oszacowane przy użyciu tego samego pomiaru.
examples.why: "przemieniające się" is the reflexive participle of "przemieniać się" (to transform/turn into), not "przemienny/komutujący" (commutative). The paragraph never otherwise explains commutation, so the reader is left with "observables that transform" instead of the commuting-operators concept. Recognizable by root, hence MINOR, but it is the term the whole admonition hinges on.

examples.source: one for each circuit being executed by the primitive / a collection of parameter values to bind the circuit against / When a circuit contains more than one classical register
examples.suggested: po jednej dla każdego obwodu wykonywanego przez prymityw / Zbiór wartości parametrów wiązanych z obwodem / Gdy obwód zawiera więcej niż jeden rejestr klasyczny
examples.translation: po jednej dla każdego Circuit wykonywanego przez prymityw / Zbiór wartości parametrów do powiązania z Circuit / Gdy Circuit zawiera więcej niż jeden rejestr klasyczny
examples.why: The English uses lowercase "circuit" as an ordinary noun, not the class name `QuantumCircuit`. Leaving it as an undeclined capitalised "Circuit" blocks Polish case inflection and reads as untranslated glossary leakage; a native technical writer would write "obwód/obwodu/obwodem" and reserve the code font for the actual class.

examples.source: *Note: These circuits must also include measurement instructions for each of the qubits to be sampled.*
examples.suggested: *Uwaga: Te obwody muszą również zawierać instrukcje pomiaru dla każdego kubitu, który ma być próbkowany.*
examples.translation: *Uwaga: Te obwód muszą również zawierać instrukcje pomiarowe dla każdego Qubitu, który ma być próbkowany.*
examples.why: "Te obwód muszą" is outright ungrammatical (plural demonstrative + plural verb with a singular noun) — the one spot where "circuit" was translated is broken. "Qubitu" is also needlessly capitalised mid-sentence; lowercase "kubit"/"qubit" is the convention used nowhere else in this file.

examples.source: a number of shots to measure the circuit with / The left-most axis of this array runs over ordered shots
examples.suggested: Use one rendering, e.g. "liczbę powtórzeń (shots)" ... "po kolejnych powtórzeniach (shots)"
examples.translation: liczbę strzałów (shots), z którą Circuit ma być mierzony / Lewa oś tej tablicy przebiega po kolejnych pomiarach (shots)
examples.why: "shots" is rendered two different ways within the same file — "strzały" (a literal gunshot calque) and "pomiary" (which collides with "measurement"/"pomiar" used for the measurement basis two paragraphs earlier). Both are glossed, so nothing is misread, but the split is exactly the within-file inconsistency an editor would unify.

examples.source: `Estimator` returns one expectation value estimate for each element of the broadcasted shape.
examples.suggested: `Estimator` zwraca jedno oszacowanie wartości oczekiwanej dla każdego elementu rozgłoszonego kształtu.
examples.translation: `Estimator` zwraca jedną wartość oczekiwaną dla każdego elementu rozgłoszonego kształtu.
examples.why: "estimate" is dropped, so the sentence claims the Estimator returns the expectation value rather than an estimate of it. The distinction is carried carefully elsewhere in the page ("oszacowania wartości oczekiwanych" in l.246/l.173), so this one is an inconsistency as well as a slightly strengthened claim.

editor_note: The prose is otherwise fluent, consistently informal ("pomoże ci", "obejrzyj", "rzuciłeś/-aś") and the core terminology is sound (qubit→qubit, superpozycja, splątanie, interferencja, bramka logiczna, obwód kwantowy), but one answer block states a factual falsehood: the English "a software development kit (SDK) like Qiskit" is rendered as "lub języka programowania, takiego jak Qiskit" — Qiskit becomes a *programming language*, a false concept for exactly the business audience this module targets (and "IBM Quantum Composer" is truncated to "IBM Composer" in the same sentence). Secondary defects: raw English glosses are injected into the prose in four places — "kwantowe bramki (Gate)", "obwody kwantowe (Circuit)" (lines 18, 142, 144, and the frontmatter description) — which appear nowhere in the English and read as a glossary leak; the scarves analogy drops the hedge "almost transparent" → plain "przezroczystymi" (fully transparent scarves would not layer to purple, breaking the analogy); and "polarized lenses" is rendered two ways one sentence apart ("polaryzacyjne soczewki" then "spolaryzowane soczewki"). Also minor: "wykładniczego paralelizmu" for "exponential parallelism" (Polish convention is "równoległość"), and the lowercase sentence-initial "qubit to podstawowa kwantowa jednostka informacji" in Key takeaways.

examples.source: We can use a visual tool like [IBM Quantum Composer](...) or a software development kit (SDK) like [Qiskit](...) to construct quantum circuits.
examples.suggested: ...lub zestawu narzędzi programistycznych (SDK), takiego jak [Qiskit](...). — and restore "IBM Quantum Composer".
examples.translation: Do tworzenia obwodów kwantowych możemy używać wizualnego narzędzia, takiego jak IBM [Composer](...), lub języka programowania, takiego jak [Qiskit](...).
examples.why: Qiskit is a Python SDK, not a programming language. The learner is taught a false concept, and the SDK notion the English is explicitly introducing is deleted. The product name is also truncated.

examples.source: Recognize the difference between quantum gates, quantum circuits, and quantum computers / Quantum circuits represent a set of instructions...
examples.suggested: Rozróżniać bramki kwantowe, obwody kwantowe i komputery kwantowe / Obwody kwantowe to zestaw instrukcji...
examples.translation: Rozróżniać kwantowe bramki (Gate), kwantowe obwody (Circuit) i komputery kwantowe / Obwody kwantowe (Circuit) to zestaw instrukcji...
examples.why: The parenthetical English glosses "(Gate)" and "(Circuit)" exist nowhere in the source; they read as an untranslated glossary leak and are applied inconsistently (absent from the body sections on the same terms).

examples.source: Imagine two friends with two very thin, sheer scarves that are almost transparent.
examples.suggested: ...z dwiema bardzo cienkimi, zwiewnymi chustami, niemal przezroczystymi.
examples.translation: Wyobraź sobie dwoje przyjaciół z dwoma bardzo cienkimi, przezroczystymi chustami.
examples.why: The hedge "almost" is dropped. Fully transparent scarves would not combine into purple, so the entanglement analogy loses the physical premise it depends on.

examples.source: ...how polarized lenses in sunglasses work. If you place two polarized lenses on top of each other...
examples.suggested: Use "soczewki polaryzacyjne" in both sentences.
examples.translation: ...jak działają polaryzacyjne soczewki w okularach przeciwsłonecznych. Jeśli położysz dwie spolaryzowane soczewki na sobie...
examples.why: The same term is rendered two ways one sentence apart, and "spolaryzowane" (polarized) is the weaker choice — the lenses polarize light, they are not themselves polarized.

examples.source: ...as far as you know each coin might be heads or tails.
examples.suggested: ...to z twojej perspektywy każda moneta może być orłem lub reszką.
examples.translation: ...to o ile wiesz, każda moneta może być orłem lub reszką.
examples.why: "o ile wiesz" is a word-for-word calque of "as far as you know" and reads as translationese; a Polish technical writer would use "z twojej perspektywy" or "z twojego punktu widzenia".

editor_note: No semantic drift: every claim, condition and quantity matches the English (including the `NoiseLearner`→EstimatorV2 / `NoiseLearnerV3`→Executor admonition, "trei cutii, dintre care două conțin adnotări `InjectNoise`", and the Pauli-Lindblad formula gloss), and the informal "tu" register holds throughout ("Poți alege", "Consultă", "Recomandăm să folosești"). What a native editor would change: (1) "circuit" is rendered two incompatible ways in the same file — capitalized/hyphenated "Circuit-uri", "Circuit-ului (Circuit-urilor) țintă", "învățat pe Circuit" in the `NoiseLearner` half (reads like an untranslated glossary token) versus the correct natural "circuite / circuitul / circuitului" in the `NoiseLearnerV3` half; (2) an outright grammar slip, "cutiile ce conțin poarte de entanglare" — the plural of "poartă" is "porți", not "poarte"; (3) "managerul de treceri boxing" is a literal calque of "pass manager" ("trecere" is the wrong sense of *pass*); (4) "utilizează ambele o componentă de învățare a zgomotului" is calqued English word order for "both utilize"; (5) a missing dative in "înainte de a fi transmis Executor", where the same file elsewhere correctly writes "Executor-ului". None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: for one (or more) circuits … that belongs to the target circuit(s) … The noise model learned on the circuit
examples.suggested: pentru unul sau mai multe circuite … ce aparține circuitului (circuitelor) țintă … Modelul de zgomot învățat pe circuit
examples.translation: pentru unul sau mai multe Circuit-uri … ce aparține Circuit-ului (Circuit-urilor) țintă … Modelul de zgomot învățat pe Circuit
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency: the first half treats "Circuit" as a capitalized English token with hyphenated Romanian endings, while the NoiseLearnerV3 half uses the normal Romanian "circuite/circuitul/circuitului". The capitalized form reads as an untranslated glossary leak, not as Romanian.

examples.source: specifies to add the `InjectNoise` annotations to boxes that contain entanglers
examples.suggested: …la cutiile care conțin porți de entanglare
examples.translation: specifică adăugarea adnotărilor `InjectNoise` la cutiile ce conțin poarte de entanglare
examples.why: "poarte" is not the plural of "poartă" (gate) — the correct plural is "porți"; "poarte" is a verb form, so the phrase is ungrammatical for a Romanian reader.

examples.source: The circuit in the previous example runs through the boxing pass manager, which groups instructions into annotated boxes.
examples.suggested: Circuitul din exemplul anterior trece prin pass managerul de boxing, care grupează instrucțiunile în cutii adnotate.
examples.translation: Circuitul din exemplul anterior trece prin managerul de treceri boxing, care grupează instrucțiunile în cutii adnotate.
examples.why: "manager de treceri" is a literal calque that picks the wrong sense of "pass" (crossing rather than compilation stage); Romanian Qiskit practice keeps "pass manager" in English.

examples.source: The error mitigation techniques PEA and PEC both utilize a noise learning component…
examples.suggested: Atât PEA, cât și PEC utilizează o componentă de învățare a zgomotului…
examples.translation: Tehnicile de atenuare a erorilor PEA și PEC utilizează ambele o componentă de învățare a zgomotului…
examples.why: "utilizează ambele" reproduces English "both utilize" word order; a native technical writer would use the "atât … cât și …" construction.

examples.source: The result of the `NoiseLearnerV3` job must be converted to a dictionary before being passed to Executor.
examples.suggested: …înainte de a fi transmis Executor-ului.
examples.translation: Rezultatul job-ului `NoiseLearnerV3` trebuie convertit într-un dicționar înainte de a fi transmis Executor.
examples.why: Missing dative marking on the indirect object; the very next sentences in the same section correctly write "îi spune Executor-ului" and "să le transmiți Executor-ului", so it is also internally inconsistent.

editor_note: Two misleading defects. (1) An entire EN paragraph from "Background" is missing: the roadmap sentence ("We end the tutorial with a discussion on other demonstrations … 15 and 21") together with the scope caveat "Note: This tutorial focuses more on the implementation and demonstration of the circuits … for an in-depth educational resource … refer to the Fundamentals of quantum algorithms course by Dr. John Watrous, and papers in the References section." The RO jumps straight from "Ultima secțiune finalizează algoritmul lui Shor…" to "### Cerințe", so the Romanian learner never gets the warning that this page is implementation-focused, nor the pointer to the course/papers. (2) In "Rulări pe hardware", DD is described as "eliminând eficient interacțiunile nedorite cu mediul și decoerența" — "eliminating" where the English says "averaging out" (and "eficient" is a false friend for "effectively"); this teaches that dynamical decoupling removes decoherence rather than averaging its effect, a strengthened claim. Supporting non-misleading defects: "gate" is rendered three ways in the same file — "Gate-uri" (l.101, 164, 271), the ungrammatical plural "poartă-uri" (l.363, 415; correct Romanian is "porți") and "porți" (l.546, 661); plus "superpozița" for "superpoziția" (l.85), "cele mai mari numărători" for "highest counts" (l.576), and mid-sentence "Backend-ul" capitalisation (l.415). Register is correctly informal "tu" throughout ("asigură-te", "Reține", "Te încurajăm").

examples.source: We end the tutorial with a discussion on other demonstrations of Shor's algorithm on real hardware … Note: This tutorial focuses more on the implementation and demonstration of the circuits concerning Shor's algorithm. For an in-depth educational resource on the material, please refer to the Fundamentals of quantum algorithms course by Dr. John Watrous, and papers in the References section.
examples.suggested:
Încheiem tutorialul cu o discuție despre alte demonstrații ale algoritmului lui Shor pe hardware real, atât implementări generice, cât și unele adaptate factorizării unor numere întregi specifice, precum 15 și 21.
Notă: Acest tutorial se concentrează mai degrabă pe implementarea și demonstrarea circuitelor legate de algoritmul lui Shor. Pentru o resursă educațională aprofundată, consultă cursul Fundamentele algoritmilor cuantici al Dr. John Watrous și lucrările din secțiunea Referințe.
examples.translation: (entire paragraph absent — RO goes directly from "Ultima secțiune finalizează algoritmul lui Shor conectând problema găsirii ordinului la factorizarea numerelor întregi." to "### Cerințe")
examples.why: A whole paragraph, including the scope caveat ('Note:') and the pointer to the in-depth course, is dropped. The Romanian learner is not told that this page deliberately skips the theory, and loses the redirection to the educational resource — a dropped caveat, not a stylistic cut.

examples.source: DD involves applying sequences of precisely timed control pulses to a quantum device, effectively averaging out unwanted environmental interactions and decoherence.
examples.suggested: …, mediind astfel efectiv interacțiunile nedorite cu mediul și decoerența.
examples.translation: Decuplarea dinamică implică aplicarea unor secvențe de impulsuri de control precise în timp pe un dispozitiv cuantic, eliminând eficient interacțiunile nedorite cu mediul și decoerența.
examples.why: 'averaging out' becomes 'eliminând' (eliminating) and 'effectively' becomes the false friend 'eficient'. The result overstates what DD does — a learner concludes dynamical decoupling removes decoherence, which is false; it averages out its coherent effect.

examples.source: a series of controlled-U1 … gates, and a layer of swap gates / report the circuit depth and gate counts
examples.suggested: o serie de porți controlate-U1 … și un strat de porți swap / numărul de porți
examples.translation: o serie de poartă-uri controlate-U1 … și un strat de poartă-uri swap / raportăm adâncimea circuitului și numărul de poartă-uri
examples.why: 'poartă-uri' is not a valid Romanian plural (the plural of 'poartă' is 'porți'); the same term is also rendered 'Gate-uri' (l.101, 164, 271) and correctly 'porți' (l.546, 661), so 'gate' appears three ways in one file, one of them ungrammatical.

examples.source: As we can see, we obtained the same bitstrings with highest counts.
examples.suggested: …am obținut aceleași șiruri de biți cu cele mai multe apariții (cele mai mari valori de contorizare).
examples.translation: După cum se poate vedea, am obținut aceleași șiruri de biți cu cele mai mari numărători.
examples.why: 'numărători' reads as 'numerators' in a mathematical text about fractions and denominators; a native technical writer would say 'apariții' or 'valori de contorizare' for histogram counts.

examples.source: we will run this circuit on the `ibm_marrakesh` backend … we transpile the circuit according to this specific backend
examples.suggested: pe backend-ul `ibm_marrakesh` … conform acestui backend specific
examples.translation: vom rula acest circuit pe Backend-ul `ibm_marrakesh` … transpilăm circuitul conform acestui Backend specific
examples.why: 'Backend' is capitalised mid-sentence (a glossary artefact); Romanian does not capitalise common nouns, and the rest of the file writes borrowed terms lowercase ('hardware-ul', 'qubiți').

editor_note: Nothing in the file would teach a learner something false — the security caveats, the trusted/untrusted-environment branch, the job-status list (QUEUED/INITIALIZING/RUNNING/DONE/ERROR/CANCELED) and the one-job-at-a-time default are all faithful, and the keep-English term convention (qubit, observable, expectation value, transpilation, error mitigation, Sampler/Estimator primitive, shot) is consistent with no ครับ/ค่ะ slips. What a native editor would change is Thai word order and a few flattened qualifiers: the English noun phrase is calqued three times as "<English> ปัญหา" ("แก้ combinatorial optimization ปัญหา", "Binary optimization ปัญหา", "combinatorial ปัญหาที่ท้าทาย classical") where Thai requires ปัญหา first — and the same row inconsistently gets it right ("ปัญหา QUBO/HUBO"). "by orders of magnitude" is garbled into "ตามลำดับตามขนาด" ("in order, by size"), which drops the magnitude claim entirely; "significantly fewer learners and a more compact ensemble" collapses to "learner และ ensemble ที่กะทัดรัดกว่า", losing "fewer"; "most informative learners" becomes "learner ที่มีข้อมูลมากที่สุด" (most data, not most informative); and "ideal entry point" is rendered "จุดเข้าถึง" (access point) instead of จุดเริ่มต้น. Also, a lost sentence break in the circuit-function table row runs "การรัน Circuit Abstract transpilation" together, and "Circuit" is capitalized mid-sentence in some rows but lowercase in others.

examples.source: Solves combinatorial optimization problems ... | Binary optimization problems or any combinatorial problem that can be mapped to a binary cost function.
examples.suggested: แก้ปัญหา combinatorial optimization ผ่านการดัดแปลง VQE quantum algorithm ... | ปัญหา binary optimization หรือปัญหา combinatorial ใด ๆ ...
examples.translation: แก้ combinatorial optimization ปัญหาผ่านการปรับตัว VQE algorithm ... | Binary optimization ปัญหาหรือปัญหา combinatorial ใด ๆ ...
examples.why: Thai puts the head noun ปัญหา before the modifier; "<English term> ปัญหา" is a raw English word-order calque and reads as broken Thai. The same table gets it right elsewhere ("ปัญหา QUBO/HUBO", "ปัญหา combinatorial"), so it is inconsistent within the file. "การปรับตัว" also means self-adjustment rather than adaptation of an algorithm.

examples.source: ... outperforming some classical solutions on supercomputers or standard SQD in convergence speed or accuracy, respectively, by orders of magnitude.
examples.suggested: ... ให้ผลดีกว่า ... ในด้าน convergence speed หรือ accuracy ตามลำดับ ถึงระดับหลายลำดับขนาด (orders of magnitude)
examples.translation: ... ทำผลได้ดีกว่าโซลูชัน classical บางอย่างบน supercomputer หรือ standard SQD ในด้าน convergence speed หรือ accuracy ตามลำดับตามขนาด
examples.why: "by orders of magnitude" is reduced to "ตามขนาด" ("by size"), which is meaningless here and silently drops the quantitative strength of the performance claim; the reader gets "better" with no sense of how much better.

examples.source: Delivers accuracy comparable to or exceeding classical models such as Random Forest or XGBoost, while operating with significantly fewer learners and a more compact ensemble. ... it selects the most informative learners
examples.suggested: ... ขณะใช้ learner จำนวนน้อยลงอย่างมีนัยสำคัญและ ensemble ที่กะทัดรัดกว่า ... เลือก learner ที่ให้ข้อมูลที่เป็นประโยชน์มากที่สุด
examples.translation: ... ขณะทำงานด้วย learner และ ensemble ที่กะทัดรัดกว่าอย่างมีนัยสำคัญ ... เลือก learner ที่มีข้อมูลมากที่สุด
examples.why: Two distinct claims (fewer learners; more compact ensemble) are merged into one, so "fewer" disappears; and "most informative" is read as "has the most data", which is a different property of a learner.

examples.source: Simplified interface for running circuits. Abstracts transpilation, error suppression, and error mitigation
examples.suggested: Interface ที่เรียบง่ายสำหรับการรัน circuit โดย abstract transpilation, error suppression และ error mitigation ออกไป
examples.translation: Interface ที่เรียบง่ายสำหรับการรัน Circuit Abstract transpilation, error suppression และ error mitigation
examples.why: The sentence break from the English is lost, so "การรัน Circuit Abstract transpilation" reads as a single garbled noun phrase and the second claim (that it abstracts away those steps) stops being a statement. "Circuit" is also capitalized here but lowercase in the neighboring rows ("parametric circuit", "deep circuit").

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the QPY compatibility caveat ("จะเข้ากันได้กับ Qiskit เวอร์ชันใหม่กว่า (แม้ว่าอาจไม่เข้ากันได้กับ Qiskit เวอร์ชันเก่ากว่าก็ตาม)") and the qpy.load caveat ("จะคืนค่าเป็นรายการของ Circuit เสมอ แม้ว่าคุณจะ serialize เพียง Circuit เดียว") keep the English's direction and emphasis, and the register is consistently informal (คุณ, no ครับ/ค่ะ). Two editorial nits, neither misleading: (1) "circuit" is rendered two ways in the same page — Thai วงจร in the title/sidebar_label ("บันทึกวงจรลงดิสก์") but bare, oddly capitalized English in every body paragraph ("บันทึก Circuit ของคุณ", "รายการของ Circuit", "โหลด Circuit ใหม่"), plus "quantum circuit" left in English at line 32; one convention should win. (2) Imperative sentences drop the Thai ให้ after หาก/เพื่อ clauses ("หากต้องการบันทึกไฟล์นี้ลงดิสก์ ใช้ฟังก์ชัน `qpy.dump`", "เพื่อสาธิต เซลล์ต่อไปนี้…"), which mirrors English word order and reads clipped rather than like native Thai instructional prose.

examples.source: Save circuits to disk / … save your circuit to file … save a list of circuits
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering: use วงจร in body prose ("บันทึกวงจรของคุณลงไฟล์", "รายการของวงจร", "โหลดวงจรใหม่") or, if English is preferred, lowercase "circuit" consistently and align the title.
examples.translation: บันทึกวงจรลงดิสก์ (title) vs. บันทึก Circuit ของคุณลงไฟล์ … รายการของ Circuit (body)
examples.why: Within-file split of the page's central noun; capitalized mid-sentence "Circuit" inside Thai prose is also a translationese tell a Thai technical writer would not produce.

examples.source: To save this file to disk, use the `qpy.dump` function.
examples.suggested: หากต้องการบันทึกไฟล์นี้ลงดิสก์ ให้ใช้ฟังก์ชัน `qpy.dump`
examples.translation: หากต้องการบันทึกไฟล์นี้ลงดิสก์ ใช้ฟังก์ชัน `qpy.dump`
examples.why: Thai instructional prose marks the imperative with ให้ after a หาก-clause; omitting it copies English word order and reads clipped.

examples.source: To demonstrate, the following cell creates a simple quantum circuit.
examples.suggested: เพื่อเป็นตัวอย่าง เซลล์ต่อไปนี้จะสร้างวงจรควอนตัมอย่างง่าย
examples.translation: เพื่อสาธิต เซลล์ต่อไปนี้จะสร้าง quantum circuit อย่างง่าย
examples.why: Bare "เพื่อสาธิต" is a calque of the sentence-initial English infinitive, and leaving "quantum circuit" in English here conflicts with วงจร used in the title.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, dropped caveats, or wrong quantities; the counterfactual "Kung naka-install ang `qiskit-toqm`, lilitaw ang `toqm`" and the three-way plugin taxonomy all match the English, and domain terms are handled with a consistent, defensible convention (English kept for plugin/pass manager/backend/synthesis/transpiler; "yugto" used consistently for *stage*, including "Mga yugto ng Transpiler"). Register is correctly casual with no po/opo. What a native technical editor would still change: (1) "para itago ang mga pangalan ng mga plugin" renders *store* with a verb whose dominant sense is "hide" — "itala"/"itabi"/"mag-imbak" is the right word for storing names in a config object; (2) the three bullets and several body sentences use the calqued "Ang X ay nagbibigay ng…" / "Ang code cell na ito ay gumagawa ng…" frame that mirrors English SVO, where native Tagalog technical prose fronts the verb ("Nagbibigay ang…", "Gumagawa ang code cell na ito ng…"); (3) the relative clause in "ipasa ang pangalan ng yugto na ang mga plugin ay gusto mong ilista" is a stiff word-for-word calque of "the stage whose plugins you want to list".

examples.source: First, create an HLSConfig to store the names of the plugins to use for various high-level objects.
examples.suggested: Una, gumawa ng HLSConfig para itala ang mga pangalan ng mga plugin na gagamitin para sa iba't ibang high-level object.
examples.translation: Una, gumawa ng HLSConfig para itago ang mga pangalan ng mga plugin na gagamitin para sa iba't ibang high-level object.
examples.why: "itago" reads first as "to hide/conceal"; the sense here is to record/keep the plugin names in a config object. "itala" (or "itabi"/"iimbak") is the natural rendering of *store* in a technical context. Recognizable but wrong-flavored — not misleading enough to fail.

examples.source: A transpiler stage plugin provides a pass manager that can be used in place of one of the 6 stages…
examples.suggested: Nagbibigay ang [transpiler stage plugin] ng pass manager na puwedeng gamitin kapalit ng isa sa [6 na yugto]…
examples.translation: Ang isang [transpiler stage plugin] ay nagbibigay ng pass manager na maaaring gamitin kapalit ng isa sa [6 na yugto]…
examples.why: All three bullets use the "Ang isang X ay + verb" inversion, a direct calque of English subject-first order. A Tagalog technical writer would front the verb; the repeated pattern across the list plus "Ang mga high-level object ay kinakatawan ng…" and "Ang code cell na ito ay gumagawa ng…" makes the page read as fluent MT rather than native writing.

examples.source: Use the list_stage_plugins function, passing the name of the stage whose plugins you want to list.
examples.suggested: Gamitin ang function na list_stage_plugins, at ipasa ang pangalan ng yugto na gusto mong ilistahan ang mga plugin nito.
examples.translation: Gamitin ang function na list_stage_plugins, at ipasa ang pangalan ng yugto na ang mga plugin ay gusto mong ilista.
examples.why: "ng yugto na ang mga plugin ay gusto mong ilista" is a word-order transfer of the English possessive relative "whose plugins"; Tagalog handles it with a resumptive "nito". Grammatical but stiff — the reader has to re-parse.

editor_note: No misleading content: the Estimator description ("Kinakalkula ng Estimator primitive ang mga expectation value ng isa o higit pang observable kaugnay ng mga state na inihanda ng mga quantum circuit"), the ISA-transpile paragraph, the PUB-tuple sentence and the Open Plan caveat ("hindi makakapagsumite ng mga session job") are all faithful, and domain terms are kept in English consistently (qubit/observable/expectation value/circuit/backend/transpiler/primitive) in the normal Taglish technical convention, with informal register held throughout (no po/opo). Three things a native technical editor would still change. In step 3, "para tukuyin ang mode na gusto mong patakbuhin nito" is a calque of "the mode you want it to run in" and reads as if the *mode* is what gets run; natural Tagalog is "kung anong mode mo gustong patakbuhin ito". In Next steps, "sa pamamagitan ng paggawa ng [Cost function lesson]" reads as "by making/creating the lesson" rather than "by working through" it. Minor: the "then" in "You can then select the QPU" is dropped, flattening the step sequencing slightly.

examples.source: use the `mode` parameter to specify the mode you want it to run in
examples.suggested: gamitin ang parameter na `mode` para tukuyin kung anong mode mo gustong patakbuhin ito
examples.translation: gamitin ang parameter na `mode` para tukuyin ang mode na gusto mong patakbuhin nito
examples.why: Calqued English syntax; as written, 'ang mode na gusto mong patakbuhin' makes the mode the thing being run rather than the Estimator. Not misleading, but no native technical writer would phrase it this way.

examples.source: Practice with primitives by working through the [Cost function lesson]
examples.suggested: Magsanay sa mga primitive sa pamamagitan ng pagdaan sa [Cost function lesson]
examples.translation: Magsanay sa mga primitive sa pamamagitan ng paggawa ng [Cost function lesson]
examples.why: 'paggawa ng' means making/creating, so it reads as 'by creating the Cost function lesson' instead of 'by working through' it. 'pagdaan sa' or 'pag-aaral ng' carries the intended sense.

examples.source: You can then select the QPU you want to use to calculate the expectation value.
examples.suggested: Pagkatapos, maaari kang pumili ng QPU na gusto mong gamitin para kalkulahin ang expectation value.
examples.translation: Maaari kang pumili ng QPU na gusto mong gamitin para kalkulahin ang expectation value.
examples.why: The sequencing adverb 'then' is dropped, so the ordering relative to initializing the account (do this AFTER) is left implicit. Mild loss of pedagogical step ordering, not a wrong statement.

editor_note: No semantic drift and nothing misleading: the plugin taxonomy, the `supports_*` reservation note, the `target`/`coupling_map`/`qubits`/`options` argument list, the `None` return caveat and the "не більше 3 Qubit" bound all match the English exactly, terminology core is correct and consistent (transpiler→транспілятор, pass→прохід, pass manager→менеджер проходів, stage→стадія, high-level synthesis→синтез високорівневих об'єктів, coupling map→карта зв'язності), and the informal "ти" holds throughout with no Ви/Ваш slips. What a native editor would still change: (1) the kept-English glossary term "qubit" is cased two ways in the same file — "вказує список qubit" (line 342) vs "фізичні Qubit" (344) and "не більше 3 Qubit" (379); (2) the third of three otherwise-identical "To check that your plugin is successfully detected" sentences leaves the link label untranslated as "[Transpiler plugins]" (line 422) while the two earlier ones render it "[Плагіни транспілятора]" (144, 313); (3) those same repeated sentences drift in wording ("Щоб переконатися, що Qiskit успішно виявляє… встанови пакет з плагіном" vs "Щоб перевірити… встанови пакет плагіна"), as do the two copies of the setuptools sentence ("дивись документацію setuptools" 311 vs "зверни увагу на документацію setuptools — там пояснено" 420); (4) minor stiffness/inexactness in "розроблено з використанням наступних залежностей" for "developed using the following requirements" (requirements ≠ залежності) and the nominalized "що означає нездатність плагіна синтезувати" for "indicating that the plugin is unable to synthesize".

examples.source: `qubits` specifies the list of qubits over which the high-level object is defined … the physical qubits in the target or coupling map … objects of type Clifford that have at most 3 qubits
examples.suggested: Pick one casing for the kept-English glossary term and use it everywhere in the file (e.g. lowercase «qubit» in all three places).
examples.translation: «вказує список qubit, на яких визначено високорівневий об'єкт» / «фізичні Qubit в цілі або карті зв'язності» / «не більше 3 Qubit»
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency in how the same glossary term is cased; the concept stays identifiable, so it is a polish issue, not a comprehension one.

examples.source: follow the instructions at [Transpiler plugins](transpiler-plugins#list-available-high-level-synthesis-plugins) for listing installed plugins
examples.suggested: дотримуйся інструкцій у розділі [Плагіни транспілятора](…) для перегляду списку встановлених плагінів
examples.translation: дотримуйся інструкцій у розділі [Transpiler plugins](…) про перелік встановлених плагінів
examples.why: The same link label is translated in the two earlier parallel sentences (lines 144 and 313) but left in English here, so the reader sees the same section under two different names.

examples.source: As before, if your project uses `setup.cfg` or `setup.py` instead of `pyproject.toml`, see the [setuptools documentation] for how to adapt these lines for your situation. (identical sentence twice)
examples.suggested: Use one wording for both occurrences (the line-311 version reads better).
examples.translation: «дивись [документацію setuptools], щоб дізнатися, як адаптувати ці рядки для твоєї ситуації» / «зверни увагу на [документацію setuptools] — там пояснено, як адаптувати ці рядки під твою ситуацію»
examples.why: English repeats the boilerplate verbatim; two different Ukrainian renderings make a reader wonder whether something different is meant.

examples.source: The code on this page was developed using the following requirements.
examples.suggested: Код на цій сторінці розроблено з такими версіями пакетів.
examples.translation: Код на цій сторінці розроблено з використанням наступних залежностей.
examples.why: «залежності» renders "dependencies", not "requirements" (the block is about pinned versions), and «з використанням наступних…» is a stiff calque a Ukrainian technical writer would avoid.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inversion, no swapped quantity, the physics (S₁/S₂, ±2 classical bound, Цірельсон bound, 63/64 pairs) all survives, and the informal "ти" register holds cleanly (Виконай, Твій час виконання, переконайся, тобі). What a native technical editor would change: (1) glossary leaks — "gate" is left untranslated and undeclined in "помилками паралельних gate" (glossary uk.json requires "вентиль"), and qubit/backend appear as capitalized English "Qubit"/"Backend" forced into inflected Ukrainian slots ("кожен Qubit", "розміщенню Qubit", "вибраного тобою Backend"), against the glossary's keep_lowercase rule and stiff to read; (2) a strengthened claim — EN "used to experimentally test Bell's theorem" becomes "для експериментального доведення теореми Белла" (prove, not test); (3) the graph-theory term "matching" of the coupling map is rendered "*відповідність* карти з'єднань" (correspondence) instead of "паросполучення", and "disjoint" as "роз'єднаних" rather than "неперетинних"; (4) "connectivity" is split within the file — "з'єднанню" in Step 2 vs. the correct "зв'язність" in the hardware section. Several calques remain ("З цими виборами", "щоб вони поділяли одне й те саме параметричне сканування", "Кожна пара відстежує ту саму синусоїду", "перехресними перешкодами" for crosstalk, the coinage "загальнопристройний"), plus a mixed conditional in "Якщо квантову механіку можна описати… ці нерівності виконувалися б завжди" (should be "Якби… можна було описати"). None of this misleads a learner, so MINOR, not FAIL.

examples.source: under realistic conditions where every pair contends with its neighbors' crosstalk and parallel-gate errors
examples.suggested: …з перехресними завадами від сусідів та помилками паралельних вентилів
examples.translation: в реалістичних умовах, де кожна пара стикається з перехресними перешкодами сусідів та помилками паралельних gate
examples.why: Untranslated, undeclinable English "gate" in an inflected Ukrainian slot — the uk glossary mandates "вентиль". "перехресні перешкоди" is also the wrong collocation for crosstalk; Ukrainian technical usage is "перехресні завади".

examples.source: The CHSH inequality … is used to experimentally test Bell's theorem (1969).
examples.suggested: …використовується для експериментальної перевірки теореми Белла (1969).
examples.translation: Нерівність CHSH … використовується для експериментального доведення теореми Белла (1969).
examples.why: "доведення" = proof. The English deliberately says test, not prove — a pedagogically meaningful distinction in a tutorial about falsifying local hidden-variable theories. Claim is strengthened relative to the source.

examples.source: we tile the backend with as many disjoint Bell pairs as its connectivity allows (a *matching* of the coupling map)
examples.suggested: …якомога більшою кількістю неперетинних пар Белла… (*паросполучення* карти зв'язків)
examples.translation: ми заповнюємо Backend якомога більшою кількістю роз'єднаних пар Белла, яку дозволяє його зв'язність (*відповідність* карти з'єднань)
examples.why: "matching" is the graph-theory term (паросполучення); "відповідність" reads as "correspondence" and makes the italicized technical term unidentifiable. "роз'єднаних" (disconnected) also mis-renders "disjoint" (sharing no qubits) — a reader could take it as "unentangled pairs".

examples.source: …conform to the instructions and connectivity supported by the target system … as its connectivity allows
examples.suggested: use "зв'язність" for connectivity in both places
examples.translation: …що відповідають інструкціям та з'єднанню, підтримуваним цільовою системою … яку дозволяє його зв'язність
examples.why: Same source term rendered two ways within the file: "з'єднання" (a connection) in Step 2 vs. the correct "зв'язність" in the hardware section.

examples.source: With those choices … so they share the same parameter sweep … Every pair traces the same sinusoid
examples.suggested: За такого вибору … щоб для них використовувалося те саме параметричне сканування … Кожна пара викреслює ту саму синусоїду
examples.translation: З цими виборами … щоб вони поділяли одне й те саме параметричне сканування … Кожна пара відстежує ту саму синусоїду
examples.why: Three English-syntax calques a Ukrainian technical writer would not produce: "З цими виборами" is a word-for-word "with those choices"; "поділяли" is the literal-but-wrong sense of "share"; "відстежує" (tracks/monitors) is a false friend of "traces" (draws out).

examples.source: If quantum mechanics could be described by local hidden-variable theories, these inequalities would always hold.
examples.suggested: Якби квантову механіку можна було описати теоріями локальних прихованих змінних, ці нерівності завжди виконувалися б.
examples.translation: Якщо квантову механіку можна описати теоріями локальних прихованих змінних, ці нерівності виконувалися б завжди.
examples.why: Mixed conditional: indicative "Якщо… можна описати" paired with a subjunctive apodosis "виконувалися б". The English is counterfactual and Ukrainian needs "Якби… можна було" to match.
